_about: Per-repo community findings (issues, PRs, discussions) mined 2026-08-18.

community.headline: microsoft/playwright-cli is public and busy: 207 issues (~240 modern ones since 2026-01) and 213 PRs, though the tracker now carries a pinned "file issues at microsoft/playwright" banner (#430) and the PR stream is almost entirely `chore: roll Playwright to ...` version bumps, so all the real signal is in issue bodies and maintainer replies, not commits. In the 2026-06-01+ window specifically the repo went quiet on features (skill-freshness notices, ESRP publishing, version rolls); the highest-value threads are slightly older but still open questions for anyone building a CDP farm. The direction of travel is explicit and maintainer-stated: headless-by-default plus a screencast dashboard (`playwright-cli show`) for human take-over, refs-not-selectors, full-detail snapshots because "1M models are sufficiently efficient", and a hard refusal to own sandboxing or containerized headful browsing ("client is responsible for the sandbox, not the tool") - which is precisely the space cuttle occupies. Four threads map one-to-one onto the user's reported pain: #325/#318 (viewer + window sizing), #317 (password values leaking into snapshots), #376 (screenshot resolution), and #252/#235 (typing mangled by argument coercion).

items.what: User running playwright-cli on a GUI-less Linux server asked how to take over the browser when the AI hits human verification. Maintainer answer: `playwright-cli show --port=0` serves the dashboard over HTTP so a remote human can drive it from their own browser. README describes what that dashboard is: a session grid with a live CDP screencast per session, and a session detail view with tab bar, back/forward/reload, an address bar, and click-into-the-viewport to take over mouse and keyboard, Escape to release.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: This is a direct alternative architecture to cuttle's KasmVNC stack (ops/docker/Dockerfile Xvfb/Xvnc/openbox + ops/docker/bin/vnc-viewer.html on :6080). A CDP screencast viewer renders the PAGE, not the X display, so it fills the panel regardless of the Chrome window size - which structurally eliminates pain point 1 (window does not fill the VNC viewer) instead of working around it. cuttle's daemon already owns every CDP session in internal/serve/pool.go and already proxies WS in wsproxy.go, so a Page.startScreencast + Input.dispatch* viewer is buildable without Xvfb. Worth at minimum as a second, lighter viewer mode alongside VNC for the remote ssh/k8s backends where VNC tunneling is the awkward part.

items.what: Feature request for a `--minimized` flag for headed sessions (headed is required to survive Cloudflare, but the window steals focus for 5-30 minute background runs). Closed NOT_PLANNED - maintainer: "We recommend using headless for these scenarios. Use `playwright-cli show` if you want to take a sneak peek." The issue body ships a complete working CDP recipe: `Browser.getWindowForTarget` then `Browser.setWindowBounds` with `windowState: 'minimized'` (or 'maximized'/'normal'), noting `--window-position=-3000,0` does not work because the OS clamps windows on-screen.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Two things. (1) The CDP `Browser.setWindowBounds` pair is the exact lever cuttle needs for pain point 1: internal/fingerprint/args.go:357 pins `--window-size` to the seed's spoofed screen (parity_test.go:220 confirms the X display is a fixed 1920x1080), so a seed with a 1366x768 persona leaves dead space in the viewer. The daemon can set window bounds post-launch per seed without touching the golden args, or the Xvfb geometry can be sized per-seed instead of fixed. (2) The maintainer's stance confirms upstream will never ship the headed-window ergonomics cuttle depends on - cuttle owns that surface alone.

items.what: `<input type="password">` values appear verbatim in the ARIA snapshot (`textbox "Password" [ref=e1612]: hunter2`). Reporter's use case is exactly a non-LLM path filling the password, then the LLM's `snapshot` leaking it to the model provider. Maintainers declined to mask password inputs: the only mechanism is `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_SECRETS_FILE` (dotenv), which redacts only values it already knows. Closed with no masking added.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's whole differentiator is the VNC handoff (internal/cli/SKILL.md "Log into a site (VNC handoff)"): the human types the password by hand in the viewer, so it is BY CONSTRUCTION not in any secrets file. The very next `snapshot` the agent runs then dumps it into the transcript. cuttle's SKILL.md secrets section (lines ~248-267) covers the download-JSON and dotenv paths but has no rule for the human-typed-in-viewer case. Since cuttle's daemon sits on every CDP connection, it could actually fix what upstream would not: strip password-input values from Accessibility/DOM responses in internal/serve, or at minimum add the SKILL rule "after a viewer login, never snapshot the login page".

items.what: Two independent reports that the CLI's argument layer mangles numeric-looking strings: `playwright-cli type "<redacted-id>"` actually typed `<redacted-id>` (leading zero silently dropped), and `playwright-cli fill e33 "<redacted-id>"` hard-errored with `'text' argument: expected string, received number` on macOS, Windows, bash and PowerShell alike, still broken several releases later.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: This is pain point 2 ("agents fumble even simple typing") with a named root cause that has nothing to do with the page: a coercion bug between the agent's shell command and the keystrokes. The affected values are exactly the high-stakes ones - OTP codes, account numbers, phone numbers, zip codes, card numbers. cuttle's internal/serve/humanize.go rewrites `Input.insertText` into per-rune keystrokes and injects deliberate QWERTY typos with correction; both paths deserve an explicit regression test for leading zeros and long digit runs, and the typo-injection should be suppressed for pure-digit fields where a corrected typo is far more damaging than for prose.

items.what: User complained every playwright-cli input command costs ~1.0-1.1s wall clock while `snapshot` costs 0.09s. Maintainer's design rationale: "Input actions deliberately waits for either network to settle or 500ms for timeouts and other asynchrony to trigger. That is still within the rounding error of your LLM completion, are you running those from a script?"
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: The single most useful maintainer comment in the repo for cuttle's humanization tradeoff. It is independent confirmation that a deliberate ~500ms-plus settle per input action is the industry-accepted cost, and that the right frame for defending it is "cheap relative to an LLM completion". cuttle's ~0.5s click (internal/serve/humanize.go pre-click settle gate sampling elementFromPoint, plus the post-click aria-toggle verify) is squarely in that budget - but note upstream settles AFTER the action on network-idle, whereas cuttle settles BEFORE on geometry. Adding a post-action network-quiet wait would close the other half and is likely a bigger reliability win than more pre-click sampling.

items.what: A contributor built and offered a Dockerfile with Xvfb + noVNC + supervisord so playwright-cli could drive a containerized headful browser over `remoteEndpoint` (PR #319, issue #329). Maintainer rejected all three stated use cases point by point: headful debugging ("we recommend running headless + use playwright-cli show to monitor w/o stealing focus"), agent sandboxing ("Client (coding agent) is responsible for the sandbox, not the tool. Moving security boundary to the tool level obscures the issue"), and corporate MITM CAs ("no security guarantees ... when running against untrusted content you need to sandbox the tool altogether").
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: This is upstream explicitly declining to build cuttle. The rejected proposal (Xvfb + noVNC + container + connect over a remote endpoint) is literally cuttle's ops/docker/Dockerfile plus internal/serve. Confirms the wedge is durable and there is no upstream roadmap collision, and the three use cases the contributor articulated (clean headful without focus theft, agent sandboxing, MITM cert injection) are ready-made positioning language for cuttle's README. The rebuttal also names cuttle's one honest caveat to document: a compromised browser in the container is not a hard security boundary for the host.

items.what: Multiple users found that pointing playwright-cli at an existing CDP endpoint on localhost:9222 silently launched a NEW browser instead of attaching (also reported against Browserbase). Maintainer: "Make sure `{ browser: { isolated: false } }` is set. CLI is isolated by default and that includes CDP. We'll consider swapping the defaults for it." Related: #209 (no docs at all on connecting to a remote CDP server) and #358 (feature request for a CDP mode, citing Vercel's agent-browser as prior art).
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: This is the single most dangerous failure mode for cuttle's entire premise. cuttle's SKILL.md says "Attach to cuttle's warm session - never launch a fresh browser or new profile", but the default-isolated behavior means an agent that gets the invocation slightly wrong gets a silent fresh browser with no fingerprint, no proxy, no logins - and everything appears to work until the site blocks it or the login is missing. cuttle's briefing (internal/cli/briefing.go) should print the exact attach invocation including whatever disables isolation, and `cuttle status` should be able to say how many external CDP clients are actually attached so the agent can verify it landed in the right browser.

items.what: `PLAYWRIGHT_CLI_SESSION=myname ... attach --cdp=http://...` fails with `Daemon pid=...: connect ENOENT myname` - the env var is misread as an endpoint rather than a session name. Only the explicit `-s=myname` flag form works with `attach`.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle hands agents a copy-pasteable attach command in its briefing. If that command uses an env var to pin the session/profile, this is a live footgun in the exact driver cuttle defaults to. Check internal/cli/briefing.go emits the `-s=` flag form, not `PLAYWRIGHT_CLI_SESSION=`, when it prints per-seed attach commands.

items.what: An agent logged in successfully, then used `open <url>` to navigate to the next page and lost its session, concluding it needed to log in again. Two causes surfaced in the thread: `open` restarted the browser (maintainer: "you are indeed correct... Open restarts the browser", fixed in v0.0.66 plus new skill files), and the coding agent had started a NEW unnamed CLI session for the second command. Fix was a combination of code change and skill-file wording.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Exactly the class of agent misbehavior cuttle's SKILL.md already anticipates ("Open your work in a new tab rather than navigating the session you are watching in the viewer"). Confirms the failure is universal across agent+CLI-browser tooling and that the fix has to live in the skill text, not only in the code. Worth checking cuttle's `cuttle open [url]` verb has an equally unambiguous rule about whether it re-navigates the watched tab or opens a new one, since cuttle's keep-alive tab (internal/serve/keepalive.go) makes the tab topology non-obvious to a driver.

items.what: A user catalogued four repeated Claude Code failure modes against the playwright-cli skill: piping snapshot output (`playwright-cli snapshot > /tmp/x.txt`) instead of using `--filename=`; inventing env vars (`PLAYWRIGHT_HEADED=1 playwright-cli open`) instead of the `--headed` flag; scattering .png/.yml artifacts into the working directory instead of the tool's own output dir; and treating `playwright-cli` as a local script file (`.claude/skills/playwright-cli/playwright-cli`) rather than a command on PATH. Recommended fix: an explicit "Don't do this / Do this instead" table in SKILL.md.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: A free list of agent failure modes to pre-empt in internal/cli/SKILL.md. cuttle is more exposed than playwright-cli on two of them: the invented-env-var pattern (cuttle genuinely does use `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_SECRETS_FILE` as an env var, so the model has evidence env vars are the idiom and will invent more), and the artifact-path confusion (cuttle's SKILL already documents that driver-written files land on the driver's host while page downloads land in the container - which is a harder rule than upstream's and therefore more worth an explicit wrong/right table).

items.what: A contributor ran a real routing benchmark on the SKILL.md `description` field: 50 prompts, skill renamed to a fictional name to defeat prior knowledge, judged by both Codex and Claude Opus. Baseline description scored 0.800 recall on Codex and 0.975 on Opus; a "Use when the user says: 'go to this URL', 'click this button'..." trigger-phrase rewrite scored 0.975 on both, with perfect precision throughout. Maintainer REJECTED it anyway: "Your description is narrowing down the set of scenarios where CLI is useful. Over-prescribing the exact scenarios might be treated as the limitation by the stronger model. As in 'use it for these exact scenarios, and these scenarios only'. As such, I prefer existing description. Models are catching up quickly."
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's SKILL.md description (internal/cli/SKILL.md line 3) is heavily trigger-phrase-loaded - it enumerates verbs and names three driver aliases. This thread is both the evidence FOR that style on weaker routers (+17.5pp recall) and the strongest counterargument against it: an over-enumerated description can read to a strong model as an exhaustive whitelist, suppressing invocation for adjacent tasks. The dual-judge methodology itself (rename the skill to a fictional name, measure recall AND a precision audit) is reusable - it is the only rigorous way to know whether cuttle's skill description is helping or capping it.

items.what: Feature request to copy agent-browser's `--interactive` (only actionable elements) and `--compact` (strip empty structural divs) snapshot filters to cut agent token spend. Closed by maintainer with a one-line rationale: "closing for now, 1M models are sufficiently efficient with the existing detail." Related: #347, where a user asked to snapshot a single ref to avoid re-dumping the whole page, and a maintainer pushed back with "What is the scenario where it is needed and cannot be just read from the previous snapshot?"; and #339 (`fileOnLargeOutput` output mode) closed NOT_PLANNED.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Useful negative signal: upstream is deliberately NOT optimizing snapshot size, betting on context windows. It means cuttle should not invest in a page-summarization or "describe the page" verb of its own on token-efficiency grounds - the driver ecosystem has already priced that in, and cuttle's job stays being the browser, not the DOM compressor. The one exception the thread does justify is scoped/element snapshots for a specific menu or dialog region, which is still a real ask that upstream declined.

items.what: Two separate reports (Windows and Azure users) that after `tab-new` or `tab-select` the printed `Page URL` / `Page Title` metadata stayed pinned to tab 0 forever, while the `Open tabs` list and the written .yml snapshot file both correctly reflected the new active tab. Reporter's own summary: "must read the generated .yml file instead of trusting the snapshot command output." Fixed in 0.1.2.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: A stale-active-target bug that makes an agent reason confidently about the wrong page - and cuttle's tab topology is strictly more confusing than upstream's, because internal/serve/keepalive.go deliberately hides an immortal keep-alive tab from drivers. Any place cuttle reorders, hides, or renumbers targets (pool.go, keepalive.go) is a candidate for the same class of defect, and it is worth a smoke-test assertion in test/smoke that the target a driver believes is current matches the target cuttle believes is current after a tab open/close cycle.

items.what: `tab-new` crashed with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '_page')` in `attach` sessions only - a plain `open` session on the same machine worked. Maintainer confirmed multi-tab support in the attached/extension path simply had not landed yet. A second commenter reported the same on Windows, wanting to work alongside the agent in the same browser window.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's ONLY mode is the attached mode - every driver reaches Chrome over CDP attach. This thread shows the attached code path in the default driver is materially less exercised than the launch path, and multi-tab in particular was broken there. It argues for cuttle's test/smoke harness to cover tab create/select/close over attach specifically, and for the SKILL to warn agents that tab manipulation is the least reliable driver surface when attached.

items.what: Detailed report of orphaned Chrome processes holding the userDataDir lock: new sessions fail with "Browser is already in use for <profile>", SAML/SSO session cookies (expires=0) die with the process forcing a re-login loop, and orphans accumulate (reporter hit 47). Maintainer flatly rejected the proposed root cause ("Root cause analysis is wrong") and the reporter's own follow-up testing narrowed it precisely: normal `session-stop` cleans up in ~1s, but SIGKILL on the daemon leaves Chrome reparented to PID 1 forever. In the parallel #360 thread another user's system was crippled by the same accumulation and they published a full workaround: a `playwright-reap` script that identifies playwright-owned processes by cmdline markers and kills only PPID==1 orphans, wired to Claude Code `Stop` and `SessionEnd` hooks plus a systemd timer backstop.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's container model already immunizes it against the accumulation half (processes die with the container) but not against the lock half: internal/serve/pool.go keeps one Chrome per seed against a persistent per-seed profile dir, so a hard-killed Chrome that leaves a stale SingletonLock will block that seed's relaunch, and the launch backoff will just retry into the same wall. Worth a stale-lock sweep on seed launch in pool.go, and `cuttle status` should distinguish "seed down, backing off" from "seed down, profile locked". The session-cookie observation is the sharper one: a Chrome restart silently drops every `expires=0` cookie, which is exactly what breaks SSO logins the user established through the VNC handoff - cuttle's CDP auth-state snapshot in internal/serve/state.go should be checked for whether it captures session cookies too.

items.what: Users asked for `--storage-state=auth.json` at open time (mirroring Playwright Test's `storageState`). Answer: the `state-save` / `state-load` commands, whose file format is the standard Playwright storage-state JSON - a `cookies` array plus an `origins` array of per-origin localStorage key/value pairs. Documented in skills/playwright-cli/references/storage-state.md, alongside first-class `cookie-get/set/delete/clear`, `localstorage-*` and `sessionstorage-*` verbs.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle already does per-seed auth-state snapshot/restore over CDP (cookies + per-origin localStorage) in internal/serve/state.go - i.e. exactly this payload, but in a private shape. Emitting and accepting the canonical Playwright storage-state JSON would make cuttle's snapshots portable: an agent could `cuttle` export a seed's state and hand it to `playwright-cli state-load`, a Playwright test suite, or browser-use, and vice versa. That is a small format change for real interop. Note upstream also exposes sessionStorage as a first-class surface, which cuttle's state.go does not capture.

items.what: A user of a third-party stealth fork of this CLI (Sekinal/stealth-browser-cli, which chains CloakBrowser -> patchright -> camoufox providers) filed a long report here by mistake: the fork silently fell back from CloakBrowser to Patchright's bundled Chromium, writing only a one-line stderr note with no underlying error, and the user ran a 40+ command research session believing they were on the stealth engine - discovering the truth only via `ps`. Once fell back, the daemon never re-evaluated the provider chain. Their asks: print the active provider and version on open, print the actual failure reason on fallback, have `list` report the real provider instead of a generic `chrome-for-testing`, add `--json`, add `goto --timeout`, and document a login-persistence recipe (`-s=<session> --persistent` + `state-save` after a manual login).
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: The strongest available evidence that stealth users demand provenance, not just stealth. cuttle spawns a self-built ungoogled-chromium 148 with a pinned 24-patch clark series (packages/browser/versions.env), and there is currently no way for an agent or user to confirm at runtime that the running binary is the stealth build rather than a stock Chrome that got substituted in an image rebuild or on a different backend. `cuttle status` and the briefing (internal/cli/briefing.go) should print engine identity - chromium version, patch-series tag, arch persona - so a silent substitution is visible in one command. The `goto --timeout` and login-persistence-recipe asks are also directly applicable.

items.what: "Unable to pass the robot verification" - a user on `open --headed --persistent` reported Google login and Cloudflare checks suddenly failing where "it was still working normally last week", and that pointing `--profile` at their real Chrome User Data directory did not help. Maintainer replied within a day: "Ouch, we'll issue an update right away." No public post-mortem of what regressed.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Independent confirmation that browser-automation stealth posture degrades silently and abruptly across upstream browser rolls, with the user discovering it only when a site starts blocking them. cuttle's defense today is the golden.json regression tripwire (internal/fingerprint/testdata/golden.json), which catches changes to cuttle's OWN output but cannot catch a detection regression introduced by a Chromium version bump in packages/browser/versions.env. The gap argues for the behavioral validate harness in packages/browser/validate/ to be run as a release gate on every engine roll, not only on patch changes - and for docs/STEALTH-VERIFICATION.md to record a dated baseline so "it worked last week" is checkable rather than anecdotal.

items.what: User automating documentation screenshots found `playwright-cli screenshot <ref>` produced exactly half the resolution of a native macOS screenshot, and that setting `deviceScaleFactor: 2` in the config file did nothing. They self-solved via `run-code` calling `page.screenshot({ scale: 'device' })` and, for a single element, `page.locator("aria-ref='e5'").screenshot({ scale: 'device' })`. The CLI subsequently shipped a first-class `screenshot --hires` flag (now in SKILL.md).
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Pain point 3 (screenshots feel like a hassle) with a precise mechanism: the default screenshot is CSS-pixel scale, so on any HiDPI persona the agent gets a soft, half-resolution image and small text becomes unreadable to vision models. cuttle pins per-seed screen geometry in internal/fingerprint/args.go and runs against a fixed 1920x1080 framebuffer, so agents are guaranteed to be in this regime. cuttle has no screenshot verb of its own and should not add one, but the SKILL.md driver-notes section should tell agents to reach for `screenshot --hires` (or `scale: 'device'`) whenever they intend to READ the image rather than just eyeball layout - a one-line docs fix for a recurring failure.

items.what: Searching every issue and PR in the repo for dialog, alert, confirm, beforeunload, cookie banner, overlay and file chooser returns essentially nothing - no user has ever complained about native JS dialogs blocking the agent. The reason is visible in skills/playwright-cli/SKILL.md: `dialog-accept`, `dialog-accept "text"` and `dialog-dismiss` are core verbs listed right next to click and fill, alongside `upload <file>`, `drop <ref> --path=`, `resize <w> <h>`, `find` (grep the snapshot with context), and `highlight <ref>`.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Directly answers pain point 4 (agents blind to native dialogs). The affordance already exists in cuttle's default driver, so this is not a cuttle feature gap - it is a routing gap: nothing in internal/cli/SKILL.md tells an agent that when clicks stop having any effect, a native dialog is the first hypothesis and `dialog-dismiss` is the probe. The stacked case the user describes (a beforeunload dialog over an app modal) is also a live hazard for cuttle's own humanization: the pre-click settle gate in internal/serve/humanize.go samples elementFromPoint in an isolated world, and a native dialog freezes JS execution in the renderer - so that gate will stall or time out rather than report the real cause. Making cuttle detect Page.javascriptDialogOpening and surface it in `cuttle status` (or in the click error) would turn an invisible hang into a diagnosable state.
items.ref: skills/playwright-cli/SKILL.md (Core commands) - and the absence of any dialog issue in all 207 issues

items.what: The canonical download answer, from the maintainer: Playwright saves downloads to a temporary location under a random name and they vanish unless you explicitly `download.saveAs(...)` after awaiting the download event, and the context must be created with `acceptDownloads`. Users repeatedly hit this as "the button was clicked but nothing downloaded". Six years later #260 asks the same thing ("Can playwright-cli download a file... say a PDF?") and the maintainer's "Yes, it can click a download link and handle the download" drew the reply "with all due respect, how? I could not locate it in the doc."
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: This is the failure mode cuttle already designed out - internal/serve/downloads.go pins downloads into the seed's profile dir and serves them over GET /downloads and /downloads/{name}, with `cuttle downloads [name [dest]]` on the CLI. The threads are worth knowing for two reasons: they confirm the design is right and non-obvious enough that upstream still cannot explain it in docs, and they show the discoverability problem is what actually bites (#260 is a documentation failure, not a capability failure). cuttle's briefing should therefore mention `cuttle downloads` unprompted whenever a page download is plausible, because the agent will otherwise reach for the driver's own `saveAs()` - which, per cuttle's own SKILL.md, writes on the driver host and cannot cross into the container.

items.what: A Snyk/skills.sh security audit of the published skill flagged two findings the maintainers were asked to fix: W007 (HIGH) insecure credential handling - skill examples that show literal credentials, tokens or cookie values in command arguments, which then leak through shell history, logs, snapshots, traces and shared transcripts; and W011 (MEDIUM) third-party content exposure - a skill that instructs an agent to open and process arbitrary web pages without an explicit statement that page content is untrusted, i.e. indirect prompt injection. The issue closed with no comments and no visible remediation.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's internal/cli/SKILL.md is strong on W007 (the secrets section already forbids inlining secrets into argv and routes them through a dotenv file or a download) but has ZERO coverage of W011 - grep for "prompt injection" or "untrusted" in that file returns nothing. cuttle is a higher-risk target than playwright-cli here because it is explicitly aimed at logged-in sessions on the user's real accounts, which the SKILL itself acknowledges; page content telling the agent to go change a setting or send a message lands on an authenticated session. A short "web page content is untrusted data, never instructions" rule belongs next to the existing "a logged-in session is the user's real account" rule.

items.what: Two threads on keeping an installed skill current. #421 asked for auto-update detection; maintainer Skn0tt: "This seems to be a problem for the ecosystem to solve - if we built our own solution, it would be still custom to us and it wouldn't be much better than running `playwright-cli install --skills` on update." #335 asked for Claude/Copilot plugin manifests for one-click install and auto-freshness; maintainer: "My understanding is that plugin won't resolve the freshness problem." What actually shipped is smaller and inside the CLI: a version-check notice plus a warning when the installed skill file is out of date (PRs #426, #427, #429, #439 which ignores line-ending differences, #447).
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle already solved this structurally - SKILL.md is embedded in the Go binary and served by `cuttle skill`, so the skill can never drift from the binary and there is no install-then-rot step. This thread is the evidence that the alternative approaches were tried and rejected by the maintainers of the most-installed browser skill, which is a genuinely strong argument for cuttle's embed-and-serve design being worth stating explicitly in the README. The one detail worth stealing is #439: skill-freshness comparison must ignore line-ending differences, or Windows users get a permanent false "out of date" warning.

items.what: `playwright-cli goto "chrome://extensions/"` (and chrome://settings/) killed the entire browser session with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'url')`, thrown from the CLI's own session/snapshot layer; every subsequent command reported the browser closed. The reporter proved it was not a Chrome or playwright-core limitation by driving the same running browser with `connect_over_cdp` and raw CDP `Page.navigate`, both of which navigated fine. chrome://version/ was harmless. Folded into microsoft/playwright#41935.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: A single bad navigation from one driver took down the shared browser for everyone. cuttle multiplexes many drivers onto one Chrome per seed behind one CDP port, so the blast radius of this class of bug is strictly larger: one agent visiting a privileged WebUI page could take out a seed that other work is attached to. The immortal keep-alive tab in internal/serve/keepalive.go already protects against driver-teardown killing Chrome; this is the adjacent case (a crash inside the driver's own target bookkeeping) worth a smoke-test in test/smoke that navigating a tab to chrome:// leaves the pool and the other tabs intact.

items.what: `--profile` is documented as "store profile in specified directory" but actually expects a Chrome User Data Directory (the PARENT of the profile folders) and always uses `Default` inside it. Pointing it at `.../google-chrome/Default` silently creates a nested `Default/Default`, and there is no way to select `Profile 2`. Closed NOT_PLANNED, so both the confusing behavior and the wrong help text remain.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's `--profile <name>` selects a seed, not a filesystem path - a completely different meaning for a flag agents have seen elsewhere. Given that agents routinely carry over conventions between similar CLIs (see #259), it is worth making cuttle's briefing and SKILL.md state plainly that `--profile` takes a SEED NAME and never a directory, and that cuttle's per-seed profile directories are managed by the daemon and not user-supplied. Also a reminder that a flag whose name matches another tool's but whose semantics differ is a reliable source of silent agent error.

community.headline: agent-browser's issue tracker (575 issues, 400+ PRs, very high traffic through Aug 2026) is essentially a public bug-bounty on exactly the four pain points cuttle has: native dialogs wedging the whole command queue, secrets/typing reliability, downloads/uploads/screenshots, and headed-window-vs-viewport mismatch. The dominant direction in the June-August 2026 window is "stop failing silently": persistent session-to-tab binding with a structured `tab_gone` error (#1589, merged), overlay hit-testing that names the covering element instead of clicking through it (#1434, merged), popup discipline that registers background tabs with a notice instead of stealing the active tab (#1657), and background target creation to stop stealing OS focus (#1695). The second theme is that a single stuck CDP call bricks the whole daemon - one hung `Runtime.evaluate`, one `Page.captureScreenshot`, or one lone UTF-16 surrogate in an AX tree takes the session down with no recovery path (#1660, #1437, #1666), which is a direct architectural warning for cuttle's single-multiplexer-per-seed design. Third, they already shipped the two affordances cuttle lacks entirely: an AES-GCM encrypted credential vault (`auth save --password-stdin` / `auth login`) whose explicit purpose is keeping passwords out of the agent's context window, and a `dialog accept|dismiss|status` verb set - and the community threads document precisely how both fall short in practice. On stealth, the maintainers never shipped it: the community's own answer is to run a stealth browser and attach agent-browser to it over CDP (#120), which is a third-party validation of cuttle's entire architecture.

items.what: Long-running report of total dialog blindness: when a page raises alert/confirm/prompt, snapshot, screenshot, click and eval all hang with a generic timeout, indistinguishable from a slow page or a dead CDP link. The reporter burned ~2h on a checkout flow before finding `dialog accept` in the README (it was absent from SKILL.md). Asks for three things: dialog verbs in the skill, a `dialog status` probe, and - the key one - rewriting the timeout error into 'JavaScript dialog is blocking: <message>'.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: This is cuttle pain #4 verbatim, with the fix already specified. cuttle has no javascriptDialog handling anywhere (grep of internal/serve/*.go finds none) so a beforeunload or app modal stalls every driver attached to that seed's port. internal/serve/wsproxy.go is the natural place: subscribe to Page.javascriptDialogOpening per page, hold the message + type in seed state, and rewrite the timeout that drivers get into a message naming the dialog. Add `cuttle dialog [accept|dismiss]` to internal/cli/commands.go and document it in internal/cli/SKILL.md - the thread proves agents never find an undocumented verb.

items.what: Minimal report that a native confirmation dialog makes agent-browser wait forever. Closed without comment - the fix was the `dialog` verb family, not detection.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Second independent report of the same class; confirms this is not an exotic edge case but the default outcome for any app with a confirm() guard. cuttle's humanize pre-click settle gate (internal/serve/humanize.go) samples elementFromPoint in an isolated world - which will itself hang behind an open dialog, so the humanization layer amplifies the wedge rather than surviving it.

items.what: `dialog dismiss` crashed with 'Unknown subcommand' while `dialog accept` worked - documented but never wired into the parser. The reporter's mental model is the interesting part: these verbs PRE-REGISTER a one-shot handler before the click that will raise the dialog, rather than reacting after the fact.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Names the right semantics for a cuttle dialog surface: a pre-armed policy, not a post-hoc rescue - because once the dialog is up, the CDP command that would arm it is already queued behind it. Suggests cuttle should default to auto-accepting beforeunload/alert at the wsproxy layer (they carry no decision) while leaving confirm/prompt to an explicit verb.

items.what: A popup whose first script synchronously calls alert() before target registration finishes wedges the opener's command lane until timeout, and later commands stay unusable. The issue body is effectively a design spec: pause new targets at browser-level auto-attach before their first script runs; auto-handle informational alert and beforeunload; keep confirm/prompt as explicit decisions; bound target init failure so it releases the command lane; never blind-accept a pre-existing dialog of unobserved type; don't leave worker/iframe targets paused.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: The most transferable artifact in the whole repo for cuttle's dialog gap - a maintainer-grade policy table cuttle can implement in wsproxy.go without rediscovering it. The auto-attach-paused pattern (Target.setAutoAttach with waitForDebuggerOnStart) is also how cuttle would keep its per-page Emulation.setLocaleOverride and focus-emulation pins from racing a popup's first script, which is a bug cuttle probably has today.

items.what:
Merged: hit-test the click point during element resolution and fail with a description of the covering element ('covered by

') instead of dispatching input that silently lands on a cookie banner, modal or sticky header. Shadow-DOM-aware relation checks and label/control association avoid false positives; the test starts from the top document so iframe content is checked in the right coordinate space.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's humanize.go already samples elementFromPoint rects in an isolated world for its settle gate and does a post-click aria-toggle re-click - it has the hit-test but throws away the diagnosis. Returning the occluder's description instead of silently re-clicking turns cuttle's blind 'agent pokes the DOM against a blocked page' failure into a one-line explanation the agent can act on, and it's nearly free given the machinery is already there.

items.what: Encrypted credential vault: `auth save <name> --url ... --username u --password-stdin` stores an AES-256-GCM encrypted profile, and `auth login <name>` replays navigate -> fill username -> fill password -> submit inside the daemon. Explicit design goal stated in #1386: 'the password never appears in the agent's context window or terminal history'. #645 documents an encryption-format split between the Node and Rust code paths that silently broke every saved profile ('Decryption failed: aead::Error').
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: This is the single biggest missing affordance for cuttle pain #2. cuttle has no secret mechanism of its own, so agents paste passwords into driver CLI args where they land in the transcript. A `cuttle secret set <name>` (env/file/stdin into the seed's daemon state) plus a `cuttle login <name>` that performs the fill server-side over CDP means the secret never crosses the agent boundary at all - and cuttle is better positioned than agent-browser because it already owns per-seed daemon state and profile dirs (internal/profile). #645 is the warning: pick ONE encryption path and one owner, never two.

items.what: The failure modes of a fixed-shape auth flow, from real users: Chinese/Asian sites default to QR login so the password form is hidden behind a click (needs `--pre-click`); Argentina's ARCA tax portal needs a click BETWEEN username and password. One user's working workaround is an `--init-script` that polls for the filled 11-digit field and clicks Next, so the vault can still be used.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: If cuttle builds server-side secret injection, do not hard-code navigate/fill/fill/submit. The evidence says the minimum viable shape is 'fill this named secret into the element the agent just identified' - i.e. a `cuttle type-secret <name> <selector-or-ref>` primitive the agent composes, not a whole login macro. That also composes cleanly with cuttle's existing humanization: the keystrokes come from humanize.go, the plaintext never leaves the daemon.

items.what: Dashboard viewport sent typed characters with ASCII charCodes as `windowsVirtualKeyCode`, which collides with Windows VK codes for every printable special character: '.' becomes VK_DELETE (deletes text ahead of the caret), '-' becomes VK_INSERT, '[' becomes VK_LWIN, ',' becomes VK_SNAPSHOT, ''' becomes VK_RIGHT. Lowercase letters (0x61+) collide with VK_NUMPAD. A confirming commenter on 0.34.0: 'a quick type hello 123 demo passes, while any password with special characters is impossible to enter'. Fix is the VK_OEM_* table (PR #1382) and deriving VK from KeyboardEvent.code, uppercased for letters (PR #1618).
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's humanize.go synthesizes real keystrokes - including rewriting Input.insertText into up to 80 runes of keydown/keyup - so it owns exactly this VK mapping table, and this bug class is invisible in testing precisely because letters and digits look fine. Audit cuttle's keycode synthesis against the VK_OEM_* table in this thread; a wrong VK on '.' or '-' is destructive (deletes/overtypes), not merely dropped, which would look to an agent like 'typing into fields is unreliable' - cuttle pain #2 exactly. The commenter's safe fallback is also worth copying: when the character isn't in the map, send windowsVirtualKeyCode 0 with `text` set - it types correctly and is never destructive.

items.what: React DraftJS editors (major social and note-taking editors) ignore document.execCommand('insertText') - text appears in the DOM but the app's state stays empty, so a submit posts nothing. Only CDP `Input.insertText` updates React's synthetic-event state correctly.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Direct hazard for cuttle's insertText rewrite in humanize.go: cuttle intercepts a driver's Input.insertText and replays it as individual keystrokes (up to 80 runes). Real keystrokes are usually MORE authentic than insertText, but this thread documents editors that specifically consume the insertText path, and cuttle's carve-out today is by rune-count and script (CJK/accents stay on insertText), not by target editor behaviour. Worth a documented escape hatch (per-seed or per-target opt-out of the rewrite) plus a note in SKILL.md, so an agent that gets a silently-empty rich-text field has somewhere to go.

items.what: Coordinate-based Input.dispatchMouseEvent clicks reported success but never fired React onClick handlers on a Material-UI FAB; eval element.click(), raw mouse down/up, focus+Enter, and 30s hydration waits all failed too. Proposal: a JS-path click via Runtime.callFunctionOn as an explicit fallback, or auto-detect React and use it.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's whole click path is coordinate-based and humanized (Fitts-law curve, settle gate, ~0.5s per click), so this failure mode lands on cuttle unchanged - and cuttle's post-click aria-toggle verify only re-clicks, it never escalates to a different mechanism. Worth adding a bounded escalation: after the aria-toggle verify still shows nothing changed, fall back once to a real element.click() and say so, rather than leaving the agent with a success it can't trust.

items.what: `fill @e1 "parth$$11"` silently entered 'parth2058111'. Root cause traced with strace: POSIX shell expands $$ to the shell PID before the CLI ever runs; single quotes fix it. Reporter's framing: 'Since the agent cannot infer that $$ is being transformed internally, it may hallucinate or retry actions unnecessarily.'
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: A pure documentation defect that costs agents entire sessions, and cuttle inherits it because every driver is invoked from a shell by an LLM. internal/cli/SKILL.md should state the rule once, next to the attach commands: single-quote any literal being typed, especially passwords - which are exactly the strings containing $, !, and backticks.

items.what: Headed mode with --start-fullscreen/--start-maximized: the configured viewport is ignored (window.innerWidth reports 800x623) and screenshots come back completely black. A commenter clarifies the model - `viewport` is a runtime CDP Emulation override, not a launch flag - and the working combination turns out to be an explicit `--window-size=W,H`; --start-fullscreen alone still black-screens.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Cuttle pain #1 in another project's words. cuttle bakes `--window-size` from the seed's spoofed screen table (internal/fingerprint/args.go:357, minus a taskbar allowance) and internal/serve/pool.go:486 explicitly refuses a passthrough override - which is correct for fingerprint fidelity and is precisely why the window can't fill the 1920x1080 VNC framebuffer. This thread confirms the two levers are independent (OS window size vs CSS viewport emulation) and that maximizing without sizing produces black captures, so the fix is not 'let the window maximize'.

items.what: PR adding `set viewport auto`, which sends Emulation.clearDeviceMetricsOverride so a headed page follows manual window resizing again. Rationale quoted: a persistent setDeviceMetricsOverride means resizing the visible window changes the window but not the CSS viewport, so the page looks clipped or stuck at an old breakpoint. Explicitly framed for 'when a human and an agent share a headed browser'.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: This is the mechanism for making cuttle's browser fill the VNC viewer without breaking the fingerprint. cuttle can keep the seed's spoofed screen metrics as the identity story while letting the actual OS window be resized to the framebuffer (via Browser.setWindowBounds) and letting the CSS viewport track it - the seed's screen.width/height spoof lives in the fingerprint layer, not in a device-metrics override. Pair with #1657's `window bounds W H` verb below.

items.what: Seven-commit production PR: (a) any response whose tab list changed carries a `tabs` field so the agent notices popups/closed/crashed tabs without polling; (b) popup discipline - pages the agent did not create register in the BACKGROUND with a notice ('New tab t4 (opened by t2) opened in background: <url>') instead of stealing the active tab; (c) refs stamped with their minting tab, so cross-tab ref use is a hard error; (d) window verbs: `window list` with bounds/state, `window bounds <w> <h> [x y]`, minimize/maximize/fullscreen/normal, and `window focus` which raises a window to a watching human WITHOUT changing the agent's active tab; (e) a headless guard because Browser.setWindowBounds{minimized|maximized} aborts headless Chrome outright.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Two things cuttle should take. First, `window bounds`/`window focus` is the missing verb pair for a VNC farm: cuttle runs headed on Xvfb with a fixed 1920x1080 framebuffer, so a `cuttle window fit` that sets the window to the framebuffer (and a focus verb that raises the right window for the human at handoff) directly answers pain #1 and makes human handoff sane. Second, the popup-notice design is the shape of a general 'out-of-band page state' channel cuttle needs anyway to surface dialogs - the agent learns about a popup or a dialog as a rider on the next command's response, with no new polling verb.

items.what: Measured focus-stealing: Target.createTarget without `background: true` is a foreground create that raises the whole browser over the user's current app, and the daemon does it on every attach, plus Page.bringToFront on every tab switch and auto-connect. Sampling the frontmost app at 150ms, Chrome took OS focus every few seconds unattended; with background:true, 0 steals out of 3. Independently reproduced on Linux/X11 with xdotool as ground truth, and both reporters note CDP docs mark `background` as Android-only while it demonstrably works on desktop.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle keeps an immortal keep-alive tab per seed and pins Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled per page so background tabs keep compositing - the same problem solved from the other end. The undocumented desktop behaviour of `background: true` is the missing half: cuttle's own internal target creates (keep-alive tab, state-save temp targets) should use it so they never raise the window in the VNC session while a human is watching another tab. Cheap, and it makes the viewer stop jumping.

items.what: `focus-emulate on/off` via Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled plus `tab new --background`, with measurements: a background tab reports visibilityState hidden and ~0 rAF ticks/s; after focus-emulate it reports visible, hasFocus() true, ~60 ticks/s, without raising the window or taking OS focus. Author is carrying it on a private fork because 'Cannot upgrade agent-browser wo these features'.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Third-party validation of a decision cuttle already made (internal/serve/serve.go:74, wsproxy.go:57 pin setFocusEmulationEnabled per page). Nothing to adopt - but the measured numbers are useful ammunition for cuttle's docs, and the fact that a production user forked upstream to get it confirms this is the right default rather than a flag.

items.what: Ten named sessions sharing one Chrome over --cdp all read back the SAME location.href: --session isolated the daemon process, not the tab, and re-attach seated the active tab at index 0 (most-recently-active). Merged fix #1589 persists a session-to-target binding, stops event-discovered targets stealing the active slot, adds `--pin-tab` strict mode that fails with a machine-readable `tab_gone` code, and accepts CDP targetIds as tab refs. Best comment, from a real-Chrome user: reads that come back wrong are recoverable, but a `click` that returns '✓ Done' after silently retargeting to a live logged-in third-party site is not - 'a ref-name mismatch was the only reason the click did not actuate a control'.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle is a multiplexer: many drivers attach to one CDP port per seed, which is structurally the same shared-Chrome topology that produced this. cuttle's keep-alive tab is hidden from drivers, but nothing binds a given driver's notion of 'the page' across a driver restart. The transferable rules are: (1) never silently re-seat a client's target, (2) when the bound target is gone, fail with a structured code plus the dead targetId and last URL as FIELDS not prose (a follow-up comment specifically asks for this - wrappers were regexing the error string), (3) expose targetIds so wrappers can key on them.

items.what: A page whose main thread never yields (or one hung Runtime.evaluate, e.g. a fetch blocked on a Private Network Access permission prompt nobody clicks) wedges the session daemon permanently: each queued CDP command burns the 30s timeout serially, killing the renderer does NOT unblock it (no fail-fast on Target.targetCrashed/detach for in-flight requests), and there is no escalation - only SIGKILL of the whole tree recovers. Also reported in the same issue: scoped snapshot is shadow-blind (DOM.describeNode without pierce:true), `>>>` piercing selectors report 'filled ✓' while changing nothing, `fill`/`type` swallow trailing --flags as literal text, and the snapshot's interactive scan MUTATES the page by tagging elements with data attributes (a real hazard on React pages).
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's serve daemon is one process fronting N Chromes on one port - a per-seed hang that blocks the shared command lane is a much bigger blast radius than a per-session daemon. Three concrete defenses to lift into internal/serve: fail all pending commands for a target immediately on Target.targetCrashed/detach; after K consecutive CDP timeouts on one target, recycle it via Target.closeTarget from the BROWSER endpoint (works without renderer cooperation, keeps the profile); and surface the hung state in the error ('target hung since T') so the driver can react instead of retrying into a black hole. The mutating-snapshot note is also a warning for cuttle's isolated-world elementFromPoint sampling - keep it read-only.

items.what: `Page.captureScreenshot` hangs indefinitely on macOS arm64 headless while open/snapshot/eval on the same page work fine; the hung capture then wedges the daemon IPC (EAGAIN, os error 35) so every later command inherits the failure, and `close --all` does not clear it - only pkill -9. Suspected software-GL compositor stall. Second commenter adds the worse variant: capturing before hydration returns a BLANK WHITE PNG rather than an error - 'silent-wrong is worse than a hang for anyone driving this from an agent loop'.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle has no screenshot verb today (pain #3), so this is a spec for the one it adds: hard-bound Page.captureScreenshot with its own timeout, never let a capture hold the shared per-seed command lane, and refuse to return an all-white/all-black frame as a success. cuttle runs headed on Xvfb with software GL, which is the exact configuration implicated here.

items.what: Screenshot with a path whose parent directory doesn't exist silently saved to ~/.agent-browser/tmp/ and printed '✓ Screenshot saved to ...' with exit 0. Reporter's framing: 'For an agent-driven tool, a false success on evidence capture is the worst-case failure mode: the agent records the check as PASS and moves on.' A second commenter couldn't reproduce on main and diagnosed the likely cause as a STALE DAEMON from an older install still servicing the socket after the CLI was upgraded.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Two rules for cuttle's future screenshot verb and its existing downloads path: an explicit path must never fall back to a default location, and the returned path must be the actual path. The stale-daemon diagnosis is separately relevant - cuttle's daemon runs in a container and can outlive a CLI upgrade the same way; a version handshake between `cuttle` CLI and `cuttle serve` would turn a class of ghost bugs into one clear error.

items.what: Feature request to scope `screenshot --annotate` to a selector: when a modal is open, a full-page annotated screenshot labels dozens of unreachable background elements, which is 'unnecessary tokens and potential confusion when selecting the correct ref' for a multimodal agent. Wants `screenshot --annotate --selector "[role=dialog]"` so labels map 1:1 to what the agent can actually click.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: The vision-side counterpart to cuttle's dialog blindness. When a page is blocked by a modal or an overlay, the useful capture is the overlay alone with its actionable elements labelled - that single image tells the agent both that it's blocked and how to get unblocked, in one turn. Good shape for a cuttle screenshot verb whenever cuttle also gains occlusion detection from #1434.

items.what: `screenshot --full` only captures the viewport when the page scrolls in an internal container (body overflow:hidden + a div with overflow:auto) rather than at document level - a very common modern layout. No fix landed.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Concrete constraint for cuttle's screenshot verb: captureBeyondViewport handles document scroll only. If cuttle offers --full it should either detect the internal-scroller case and say so, or scroll-and-stitch the container - silently returning a viewport-sized image labelled 'full page' is the same false-success class as #1534.

items.what: Three separate download failures with one shared root cause - download behaviour is configured once, per-context, and nothing re-applies it. #1300: `wait --download <path>` reports the requested path in JSON (data.path, savedFilePath, savedFile.path all agree) while the file actually lands in ~/Downloads. #1018: `record start` creates a fresh BrowserContext and never re-applies Browser.setDownloadBehavior, so every download after recording starts is silently dropped (headless denies downloads by default). #1659: on Windows, Rust's canonicalize() produces a \\?\ verbatim path that Chrome accepts in setDownloadBehavior but then cancels every download for - and the cancellation only surfaces later as a downloadProgress state:'canceled' event, making it near-undiagnosable.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle pins downloads into the seed profile dir and serves them over GET /downloads (internal/serve/downloads.go), which already sidesteps the path-lying problem - but only as long as the pin survives. The transferable lessons: re-apply setDownloadBehavior on every new context/target (cuttle blocks Target.createBrowserContext by default, but --allow-context-creation opts out and would break the pin), subscribe to Browser.downloadProgress and surface the 'canceled' state instead of letting a download vanish, and verify the file exists before reporting success.

items.what: Upload is imperative (requires a selector for the <input type=file>) where Playwright MCP's is reactive (detects the open file chooser and takes paths). Dynamically-created inputs - `document.createElement('input'); input.click()` - have no selector at all, so agent-browser simply cannot upload on those sites. #1107 adds that `upload` uniquely rejected accessibility refs that fill/click accept. #192 notes the native OS picker cannot be closed programmatically and blocks everything behind it, including in headless.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle has no upload support at all, and the same native-picker dialog is a first-class member of cuttle's pain #4 (invisible native window over a blocked page). The right primitive is Page.setInterceptFileChooserDialog + Page.fileChooserOpened + DOM.setFileInputFiles at the wsproxy layer: the picker never opens, the agent calls `cuttle upload <path>` after the click that would have opened it, and dynamically-created inputs work because the interception is on the chooser event, not on a selector. This is one of the cleanest wins available to cuttle - it removes a whole blocking-dialog class rather than handling it.

items.what: Detailed report that snapshot refs are POSITIONAL within the latest snapshot, so a ref remembered from an earlier snapshot silently actuates whatever element now occupies that number after a DOM insertion - with a 5-command data: URL repro (click @e2 clicks Alpha instead of Beta and reports '✓ Done'). Real-world receipt: combobox widgets insert a node per committed selection, shifting every later ref, and 'this mechanism shipped wrong category selections to multiple live product-directory listings, each wrong click acknowledged with ✓ Done'. Proposed fixes: mint refs against backendNodeId, or stamp a snapshot epoch and reject stale-generation refs with a teaching error. #1504 asks for the same 'fail loudly'. #1351 quantifies the tax: an E2E agent measured +65% LLM turns vs Playwright MCP, ~30% of tool calls being defensive re-snapshots.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle doesn't own the snapshot layer - the drivers do - so this is not a cuttle bug. But it is the single biggest driver of agent turn count and wrong-action risk on top of cuttle, and cuttle's SKILL.md is where the mitigation lives: re-snapshot immediately before each actuation on dynamic UIs, prefer stable selectors over remembered refs, and use the #853 tab-isolation pattern below. Also a design constraint if cuttle ever adds its own describe-the-page verb: bind refs to backendNodeId and fail stale ones loudly, never renumber positionally.

items.what: A field-tested SPA scraping pattern with measurements: never navigate the source tab. Clicking into a detail page and hitting back() makes Google Maps re-render the feed and reassign every ref (Hostel Siri e36 -> e28), so sequential extraction fails from item 3 onward. Opening each detail in an ephemeral new tab and closing it keeps tab 0's refs stable: 5/5 items vs 2/5, then 70+ records across 14 cities in 19 minutes with zero errors.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Ready-made, evidence-backed guidance for internal/cli/SKILL.md - it costs nothing to include and it converts the most common multi-item extraction failure into a working recipe. It also composes with cuttle's architecture: cuttle already keeps a hidden keep-alive tab and pins focus emulation per page, so ephemeral background tabs stay fully operable, which is exactly what this pattern needs.

items.what: The 13-comment stealth thread the maintainers never shipped. Community consensus, from someone running it in production: puppeteer-extra-plugin-stealth bypasses Cloudflare Turnstile reliably only when combined with headless:false ('critical - CF detects headless even with stealth'), --disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled, a system Chromium channel rather than the bundled one, and a persistent context. Another proposes making the driver pluggable via env var so patchright/camoufox can be dropped in. The endpoint of the thread is the important part: run a stealth browser as a container exposing CDP on 9222 and just `agent-browser connect 9222` - with a bot.sannysoft eval snippet reporting 56/56 passed. On #506 (Cloudflare) the highest-signal reply is 'this is a proxy and/or fingerprint issue. Works fine with a good fingerprint + proxy.'
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: This is an independent, three-year-running argument for cuttle's exact architecture: headed real browser + patched engine + fingerprint + proxy, fronted on a CDP port, with the driver as a separate replaceable thing. Two operational takeaways: keep and publicise the headed-on-Xvfb decision as a stealth requirement rather than a container inconvenience, and steal the bot.sannysoft one-liner eval (returns {passed, total} plus the failing rows) as a cheap smoke check to sit alongside docs/STEALTH-VERIFICATION.md. It also names the demand cuttle is positioned to capture: these users want a stealth CDP endpoint, not a stealth plugin.

items.what: Long thread on attaching to a user's already-running Chrome for login reuse, with two high-signal comments. One explains why an extension path cannot be retrofitted onto a CDP tool: CDP binds at the browser-process level and Chrome M136+ refuses it on a real user profile because that would defeat Safe Storage HMAC isolation, whereas native messaging runs as a child of Chrome and inherits cookie/SSO state - 'not interchangeable transports, different control planes with different capability sets (no CDP-class network interception, isolated worlds)'. Another explains why you cannot just copy a live profile: Cookies DB writes, LocalStorage flushes and Preferences rewrites are in flight, so you get a corrupted copy - snapshot-then-launch is the only consistent pattern. Related: #1502, --profile on macOS launches Chrome for Testing which reads the wrong Safe Storage keychain key, so no login is reused at all.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Validates cuttle's per-seed profile store and its CDP-level auth-state snapshot/restore (cookies + per-origin localStorage) as the right design rather than a compromise - and explains why 'just point it at my real Chrome profile' requests should be declined on the record. The live-profile-copy hazard is worth stating in cuttle's docs, and the Safe Storage detail is a concrete reason cuttle's snapshot-over-CDP approach beats file-level profile copying.

items.what: Session-state restore installs a Fetch interception that serves <html></html>, which can race live page loads and hand HTML to script requests, producing 'SyntaxError: Unexpected token <' in the page. Related: #1505, auth-state loading fails when one sessionStorage key holds an abnormally large value; #1441, a custom executable path silently disables state restore (save works, restore doesn't).
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle does per-seed auth-state snapshot/restore over CDP (internal/serve/state.go) using the same about:blank-per-origin trick these bugs come from. Worth auditing directly: scope any Fetch/request interception used during restore to the synthetic navigation only and tear it down before real loads, bound per-origin storage size, and make a restore that cannot run fail loudly instead of leaving the seed logged out with a green exit code.

items.what: With the default idle timeout, a session closes itself while a human is watching it in the dashboard's live view - only commands or input reset the timer, so watching doesn't count as activity. Sibling issue #1536 documents the opposite failure with receipts: no idle timeout by default leaks daemons and full Chrome trees for days (one leaked renderer at 100% CPU for 2 days, 7.8GB RSS; another workstation with 143 Chrome processes across 11 profiles, oldest 10 days), and a commenter names the reason integrators never set it: '--session <name> reads as a namespacing flag. Nothing at the call site suggests it allocates a process tree with a lifetime you now own.' Killing a daemon is also how orphans get made - a timeout needs a live daemon to fire it.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Both halves land on cuttle. cuttle's whole human-handoff story is a person watching KasmVNC at :6080 solving a captcha - if any idle reaping ever ships in internal/serve/pool.go, an attached VNC viewer must count as activity, or cuttle will kill the browser mid-captcha. And the leak side is the argument for reaping at all, plus for cuttle's supervise.go owning the Chrome tree so an orphan cannot outlive the daemon.

items.what: Stream frame metadata substitutes the CONFIGURED viewport for the real CDP deviceWidth/deviceHeight, so remote clicks land off target: a browser launched at --window-size=1280,720 has a 1280x633 content area, and every Y coordinate gets stretched by 720/633 - a click aimed at (320,158) dispatches at (320,180), with error growing linearly down the page. Verified with a standalone repro script printing real vs advertised vs frame-metadata dimensions.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's viewer is KasmVNC streaming a real X server, so the pixels a human clicks are genuinely the browser's - this specific bug doesn't reproduce. But the invariant behind it is exactly cuttle pain #1: the browser window occupies only part of the 1920x1080 framebuffer because --window-size is derived from the seed's spoofed screen minus a taskbar allowance, so a human sees a window floating in dead space. The lesson to carry over is to publish the real content-area dimensions (and the window's position within the framebuffer) somewhere the agent and any future overlay can read, rather than assuming the configured size is the truth.

items.what: Live-view input fixes with measurements: every input event awaited Chrome's (dataless) reply before the next was read, so a mouse sweep's 60-125 events/s serialized a following click behind seconds of backlog - dispatch-without-await plus coalescing mouse moves to ~25/s took a 300-event sweep-then-click from ~5s to ~35ms. Ctrl+letter shortcuts were no-ops because VKs came from charCodeAt on the lowercase key, and combos were sent with `text` (which Chrome treats as typing, not a command). Plus a full clipboard bridge: Ctrl+C mirrors the remote clipboard locally, Ctrl+V reads the local clipboard and inserts at focus, with clipboard-read/write permissions granted at screencast start and slow reads moved off the frame path. A commenter adds that the viewport's capture-phase keydown handler calls preventDefault on every key, so the page never even receives a paste event.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: KasmVNC gives cuttle real X-level input and its own clipboard channel, so most of this is already solved by construction - which is itself worth knowing (it's a genuine advantage of the VNC approach over a screencast canvas). The part that does transfer is the human-handoff secret path: pasting a password or a 2FA code into the browser during handoff must actually work end to end, and the clipboard is the natural carrier for a secret the agent must never see. Verify cuttle's KasmVNC clipboard round-trips both directions before relying on it.

items.what: An agent navigated away from a user's live pfSense admin session because the skill's examples used the default session, and the daemon persists across conversations. The fix was documentation, not code: the maintainers' merged session-binding PR #1589 lists 'Skill docs require a named session up front, so parallel agents stop colliding on the default'. Commenter: 'The current official SKILL.md uses the default session in all examples, which is the source of the problem.'
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: A clean case of an LLM misbehaving because the skill's examples taught it the wrong default, fixed by changing the examples. cuttle ships an embedded internal/cli/SKILL.md and `cuttle up` prints the live briefing with attach commands - which means cuttle controls exactly this lever. Audit the briefing and SKILL.md so every printed example is the safe form (explicit seed/context, never an implicit shared default), because agents copy the first command they see verbatim.

items.what: snapshot hangs forever when the accessibility tree contains a lone UTF-16 surrogate (a flag emoji): the CDP response is silently DROPPED in the reader loop, so the caller waits on a reply that will never come. Sibling defects in the same family: #1666's reader loop, and #1692 where the plain-text renderer reads err.get("message") while the producer emits {text,url,line,column}, so unwrap_or("") turns a missing key into an empty string and every error message renders as a bare '✗'.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's wsproxy is a JSON-rewriting CDP proxy - it parses, mutates and re-emits every message on the path (context blocking, param stripping, insertText rewriting, focus pins). Any message the proxy fails to parse or re-encode, including one carrying an unpaired surrogate from a page's own text, must be passed through or must fail loudly - silently dropping a CDP response hangs the driver with no diagnosis, which is the hardest possible bug to attribute to the proxy. Worth a targeted test in wsproxy_test.go with invalid-UTF-16 payloads.

items.what: Demand for CDP BrowserContext isolation so parallel agents on one Chrome get separate cookie jars in ONE process and ONE window (context creation ~5ms vs a full Chrome launch per session), with a comparison table arguing contexts beat per-session profiles on window count, process count and startup time. A community PR implementing --context was closed; the request is still open with follow-on '+1, this is quite important'.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle deliberately blocks Target.createBrowserContext (internal/serve/wsproxy.go:450, 'one identity per seed') and strips identity params from any that get through under --allow-context-creation. This thread is the counter-pressure cuttle will keep meeting, and it is worth having the answer written down: for cuttle a context cannot pick its own fingerprint/proxy/geo because identity is a launch flag, so cookie isolation without identity isolation is a stealth trap, and the seed IS the isolation unit. Watch, don't adopt - but expect the ask.

items.what: Unknown --flags are consumed as positionals, so `screenshot --full-page` writes a FILE NAMED '--full-page' instead of erroring. Same family as #1660 item 4, where `fill #a hello --timeout 2000` types the literal string 'hello --timeout 2000' into the field, and #1645, where `errors --clear` is a silent no-op because the daemon ignores the flag.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: A recurring agent-ergonomics pattern worth encoding as a rule in cuttle's CLI: an unrecognised flag is an error, never a positional, and never a silently ignored no-op. LLMs guess flag names constantly (they hallucinate --full-page from Playwright), so the CLI's response to a guessed flag is a first-class part of the agent interface - a clear rejection costs one turn, a file named '--full-page' costs a debugging session.

community.headline: CloakBrowser is a very active public repo (30.3k stars, ~500 issues, 27 discussions, maintainer "Cloak-HQ" answering nearly every thread with real root-cause detail) and its conversation history is essentially a field log of the exact problems cuttle has. Architecturally it is cuttle's mirror image: stealth patches live in the Chromium binary, but humanization lives in a Python/JS *wrapper* that monkey-patches Playwright - so it evaporates the moment anyone attaches over CDP (#126), which is precisely the gap cuttle closed by humanizing inside the daemon. The most valuable artifacts are the maintainer's design explanations (why exposeFunction/onConsole stay disabled, why screen size is fixed per platform not per seed, why an external --remote-debugging-port breaks a Playwright-managed browser) and a cluster of humanize bugs cuttle has structurally inherited: stale isolated-world context after navigation (#507, #108), settle-gate not re-scrolling after the wait and silently "succeeding" on a click that never lands (#329), and iframe actions resolved against the top frame (#428). On cuttle's four named pain points: window-fills-the-viewer has a shipped binary-level answer (#99 - spoof window.screenX/Y from the seed so the real window can sit at 0,0 filling the Xvfb display); agent-ergonomics has a well-specified unbuilt CLI request (#274) plus live MCP demand (#206); and native dialogs are confirmed *unsolved by anyone* - #504 sat unanswered since August with the reporter having exhausted flags, Playwright route(), and Chrome Enterprise Policy.

items.what: Binary-level patch that spoofs window.screenX/window.screenY from the fingerprint seed, so the real OS window can sit at 0,0 and fill the whole Xvfb/noVNC framebuffer while JS reports a randomized, stable-per-seed position. Shipped after a user pushed back on the --window-position workaround: 'If you use --window-position arg currently with xvfb there will be deadspace.'
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: This is cuttle pain #1 with a known fix. internal/fingerprint/args.go:357 emits --window-size=<seed screen width>,<height-taskbar>, so a 1366x768 seed leaves most of the fixed 1920x1080 VNC framebuffer empty. Decoupling the real window geometry from the reported geometry (screenX/Y here; outerWidth/outerHeight/screen.* would need the same treatment) is what lets cuttle maximize the window in the viewer without breaking seed coherence. cuttle's patch series is forked from clark and already carries fingerprint switches (packages/browser/patches/000-shared/clark_fingerprint_switches.cc), so this is an additive patch in familiar territory.

items.what: Maintainer's stated design rule: screen dimensions are FIXED per platform (Windows/Linux 1920x1080, macOS 1440x900), never randomized per seed - 'Randomizing screen size would actually increase fingerprint uniqueness, making each session more identifiable rather than less.' Separately, #325 shows a user hitting exactly the mismatch and self-solving with --window-size=1920,1080.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle does the opposite: internal/fingerprint/args.go has a per-seed screen table, which is both the cause of the VNC dead space and (per this maintainer's reasoning) a possible uniqueness liability. Worth a deliberate decision rather than an inherited one - and note that the golden at internal/fingerprint/testdata/golden.json pins seeds to 1366x768 / 1440x900 / 1920x1080, so any change is a conscious golden regeneration.

items.what: Regression report + maintainer fix: the humanize layer's pre-action checks were bound to an isolated world refreshed only on page.goto, so a navigation driven by a click or form submit left them pointed at the previous (bfcached) document and every fill() threw ElementNotAttachedError. Fixed by refreshing the checks on EVERY main-frame navigation, not just goto. In #108 the same maintainer had already warned: 'the execution context ID is invalidated on navigation, so you'll need to recreate the isolated world after each page.goto()'.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle has this bug today. internal/serve/humanize.go:998 isolatedWorld() caches the executionContextId per session in h.worlds[sid] and never invalidates it - there is no Page.frameNavigated / Runtime.executionContextDestroyed handling anywhere in internal/serve/. After the first navigation the cached id is stale, every probe Runtime.evaluate fails, and because awaitStable is documented as a 'fail-open settle gate' the pre-click settle and the post-click aria-toggle verify silently stop working for the rest of the connection - degrading to bare clicks with no diagnostic.

items.what: Feature request for isolated-world evaluation, answered with a maintainer-verified detection table. Main-world page.evaluate leaks 'at eval (eval at evaluate (:302:30))' in Error.stack - a known automation fingerprint - while Page.createIsolatedWorld + Runtime.evaluate produces 'at <anonymous>:2:19', is invisible to page monkey-patches of addEventListener, and keeps variables isolated in both directions. Reporter's follow-up table confirms elementFromPoint works fine in the isolated world and DOM reads trigger no MutationObserver.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Independent third-party confirmation that cuttle's design choice in internal/serve/humanize.go (probeExpr/elementFromPoint sampling in a private 'cuttle_probe' world rather than the main world) is the correct stealth call, with the specific vectors enumerated. Also names the exact caveat cuttle has not handled - navigation invalidation - and the addEventListener-override invisibility property, which is a good line for internal/cli/SKILL.md when explaining why cuttle's clicks are safer than a driver's page.evaluate.

items.what: Bug in the settle gate: when a page kept reflowing after an element was scrolled into view, the wrapper waited for position to settle but did NOT re-scroll, so the element got pushed out of view and the stable check failed forever - 'or, worse, a click landed on nothing while reporting success.' Fix: re-scroll into view after the settle wait, AND make a click that genuinely cannot land raise instead of passing silently.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Maps one-to-one onto internal/serve/humanize.go awaitStable() (line ~782), which is explicitly a fail-open gate: at budget exhaustion it returns toggleOf(cur) and presses anyway. On an infinite-scroll or lazy-loading page that is the exact 'click lands on nothing, reports success' failure this issue describes - and it is invisible to the agent, which then poke-loops the DOM. Two changes: re-sample-and-re-scroll inside the gate, and surface a real CDP error on a click the gate could never stabilize.

items.what: With humanize on, Locator actions on elements inside an iframe resolved against the top-level document instead of the owning frame, throwing ElementNotAttachedError; frame-level methods had the same bug. Fixed in PR #429 so sub-frame click/fill/hover/type resolve in the owning frame's own document with humanized mouse motion preserved inside the frame.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's createWorld() (internal/serve/humanize.go) calls Page.getFrameTree and creates the isolated world only for frameTree.frame.id - the MAIN frame. Any click whose target lives in an iframe (consent CMPs, captcha widgets, embedded payment and login forms - i.e. most of the hard cases) has its elementFromPoint probe evaluated in the wrong document, so the settle gate and toggle-verify silently no-op there. Needs per-frame isolated worlds keyed by the frame under the cursor.

items.what: Native 'Open xdg-open?' external-protocol confirmation dialog appears on Linux and blocks/pauses the page's JS execution. Reporter exhausted --disable-features=ExternalProtocolDialog, Playwright context.route() aborting the scheme, and Chrome Enterprise Policy AutoLaunchProtocolsFromOrigins via /etc/opt/chrome/policies/managed/policy.json. Filed 2026-08-13, still zero replies including from the maintainer.
