items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: This is cuttle pain #4 with hard evidence that nobody in the ecosystem has an answer, and it names the mechanism precisely: the native dialog is a browser-chrome window, so it is invisible to every DOM/route-level technique and it stalls the page's JS - which is exactly why an agent keeps poking a blocked page. grep confirms cuttle has no Page.javascriptDialogOpening / Page.handleJavaScriptDialog handling anywhere in internal/serve/. A daemon-side dialog observer (auto-Page.enable per page, report open dialogs in status, expose a dismiss verb) would be a genuine differentiator, not a catch-up feature.

items.what: The single highest-signal architectural thread in the repo. humanize=True has no effect when connecting over CDP, because the behavioral layer is a wrapper monkey-patch of Playwright's page.click/fill/mouse, not part of the binary. A user spells out the ideal workflow: 'CloakBrowser launches once with humanize: true and stays alive. Multiple external scripts connect to it via CDP, each reusing the same humanization layer... Currently, CDP gives me stealth flags but not humanization - so I lose the very feature that makes CloakBrowser special.' The maintainer's answer was an escape hatch (a cloakbrowser/human import you apply to a CDP-connected Browser), not a daemon-side fix.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Direct third-party validation of cuttle's core architectural bet: humanizing CDP Input inside internal/serve/humanize.go means agent-browser, browser-use and playwright-cli all get behavior for free, in any language, with no per-driver patching. It also names the failure mode cuttle avoided - every driver needing its own maintained fork of the humanization logic. Worth stating explicitly in internal/cli/SKILL.md and the README as the reason cuttle is a multiplexer and not a library.

items.what: Maintainer's behavioral-gap playbook, written for a user whose form submission passed when driven by hand and failed when automated on the identical browser + proxy session. The rules: use page.type() not page.fill() ('sets the value with no keystrokes, an instant behavioral flag'); use selector methods not page.query_selector() ('ElementHandle objects bypass all humanize patches, so the mouse teleports and keystrokes fire with no timing'); and 'use time.sleep(), not page.wait_for_timeout() - the latter sends CDP commands that get detected.' Issue #65 is the same guidance as a standalone method-by-method table.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle already neutralizes the first two structurally - humanize.go rewrites Input.insertText into real keystrokes (up to 80 runes) at the CDP layer, so an agent that calls fill() gets keystrokes anyway, and ElementHandle vs Locator is irrelevant because interception happens below the driver. That is a concrete, quotable advantage over the wrapper approach and belongs in internal/cli/SKILL.md. The wait_for_timeout claim is the one cuttle does not cover and is worth verifying - if true it is a per-driver guidance line for the skill.

items.what: Three humanize ergonomics bugs confirmed by the maintainer in one reply: (1) the element-box lookup hardcodes timeout:2000 and ignores the caller's timeout, so page.click(sel, {timeout: 5000}) still fails at 2s; (2) typing config is frozen at patch time, so you cannot type an email fast and a password slowly, or disable typo injection for one field - fix was a per-call human_config override; (3) scrollIntoViewIfNeeded was never humanized.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: internal/serve/humanize.go is all package-level constants (fittsA, prePressMs, queryTimeout, gateBackoff). cuttle has no per-action override channel at all, and its cost profile (~0.5s per click, ~130ms/char) makes the second point acute: a 40-character secret costs 5+ seconds of typo-injecting keystrokes into a password field where typos are actively harmful. A per-seed or per-request speed/typo dial (query param on the CDP attach URL, matching how cuttle already passes fingerprint) is the cheap version.

items.what: Maintainer explains that Playwright-driven downloads land under a temporary random filename with NO extension by design (upstream microsoft/playwright#24048, #9279); the real name exists only as download.suggested_filename and you must call download.save_as() yourself. Related #335: after changing the download directory the file cannot be found in the target folder at all, and the native right-click context menu 'flashes/flickers instantly, making it impossible to display or use'.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle sidesteps the naming half by pinning Chrome's own download.default_directory + prompt_for_download:false in the profile Preferences (internal/serve/pool.go pinDownloadDir), so Chrome-native downloads keep real filenames for GET /downloads. But a Playwright driver attaching with acceptDownloads sends Browser.setDownloadBehavior with its own downloadPath and overrides that pin - producing GUID-named files outside the seed dir and an empty /downloads listing. Worth a smoke test in test/smoke and, if it reproduces, intercepting/rewriting setDownloadBehavior in the multiplexer the way cuttle already rewrites other CDP traffic. The #335 context-menu flicker is also a headed-Xvfb/openbox artifact cuttle's ops/docker stack could hit.

items.what: A well-specified request for a thin agent-facing CLI, explicitly scoped to not replace Playwright: cloakbrowser doctor --json, profile list, profile path <name>, open --profile --url, screenshot --profile --url --out, dump inputs|buttons|text --json, eval --js-file --json. Framing: 'For humans this is manageable, but for agents and automation pipelines, a stable CLI is much easier to compose and reuse than ad hoc scripts.' Maintainer: 'we see the value in a thin CLI layer for agent workflows.'
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: This is cuttle's verb list (up/down/status/open/downloads/logs/purge-profile/context/skill) with the three gaps the user reports named independently: screenshot, dump (a machine-readable 'what is on this page' - inputs, buttons, text), and doctor --json. `dump` in particular is the antidote to pain #4: an agent that is blind to a native dialog at least learns from `cuttle dump` that the page has zero actionable inputs, instead of poke-looping. The scope discipline in this issue ('no workflow DSL, no site-specific automation') matches cuttle's KISS/YAGNI non-negotiables.

items.what: Sustained demand for an MCP server (issue #206 plus Ideas discussion #212, multiple +1s). Maintainer's answer: it already works by pointing the official Playwright MCP at the stealth binary (npx @playwright/mcp --executable-path ...), and floated a dedicated package adding preconfigured stealth args, geoip auto-detection, humanize, and simplified setup. A community member shipped swimmwatch/cloakbrowser-mcp as exactly that thin bridge. One user's LLM 'didn't know what to do with it' over streamable-http and screenshots came back empty - a transport/config problem, not a browser problem.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's answer today is internal/cli/SKILL.md plus third-party driver CLIs, which is a deliberate and defensible choice - but this thread shows the demand is real and that the winning shape is a thin bridge over an existing MCP, not a new automation surface. It also documents the failure mode to design against: an agent handed an unfamiliar tool surface flails, which is the same class of problem as cuttle's pain #2 and #3. Worth deciding explicitly whether SKILL.md is the permanent answer.

items.what: Two independent requests for a visible mouse cursor so a human can watch what the automation is doing, both still unanswered. The discussion names the trap: 'I'm stuck with injecting it when the page loads but that can be caught with CDP detections.'
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's whole differentiator is the KasmVNC human-handoff viewer, and it moves a Fitts-law curved mouse with tremor that a watching human currently cannot see - the pointer is invisible in the VNC framebuffer during CDP-synthesized input. The trap identified here is exactly the one cuttle must avoid: do NOT inject a DOM cursor (page-observable). Render it in the X11/VNC layer instead, where cuttle already owns the stack (ops/docker Xvfb + openbox + KasmVNC). That makes the humanize layer legible during handoff and turns a hidden mechanism into a demo.

items.what: Exhaustively-diagnosed silent failure: the browser launches, is_connected() returns True for ~1-2s, then the first page.goto() throws a generic TargetClosedError with no explanation anywhere. Root cause was a session-cap denial. Maintainer's key admission: 'The binary does report a clear reason... The problem is that Playwright owns the launch and swallows that exit reason, so all you see is the generic TargetClosedError on your first call. The fix belongs in the wrapper.' The reporter had ruled out Defender, ASR, AppLocker, SmartScreen and crash dumps before filing.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's pool has launch backoff (internal/serve/pool.go) and a supervise loop, and a driver attaching over CDP to a seed whose Chrome failed or is backing off will see the same content-free 'Target page, context or browser has been closed'. An agent cannot recover from that message - it retries the same broken thing. The lesson is transferable regardless of cuttle having no licensing: whatever the daemon knows about why a seed's Chrome is not usable (exit code, backoff remaining, crash) must reach the attaching client as a real error, and `cuttle status` should show it. Cheap, and it removes a whole class of agent flailing.

items.what: Two linked reports (Windows native, no proxy) that only the FIRST page of a persistent context behaves: the startup page renders and completes fingerprint.com's full server-side JSON, while context.new_page(), ephemeral contexts, and manually opened tabs render partial HTML with the load indicator spinning forever and fingerprinting pages never completing. In #254 a user reports 'only the first two tabs can open the webpage normally; any pages beyond that are blank.' Neither is resolved.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's architecture makes exactly this class of bug likely and hard to see: an immortal keep-alive tab hidden from drivers, plus a per-page Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled pin applied on page creation. If the pin (or the Emulation.setLocaleOverride) is applied to some pages and not others, or races page creation, cuttle gets divergent first-page-vs-later-page behavior with no error. Worth an explicit N-tab test in test/smoke asserting that page 1, page 5 and a window.open popup all reach the same state - popups in particular, which never appear anywhere in these threads and are the tab-management case nobody has tested.

items.what: Detailed report that playwright.chromium.connect_over_cdp against the cloakserve multiplexer hangs on the FIRST CDP frame across every release 0.3.20-0.3.30, while raw websockets-library CDP clients work on the same endpoint in 40ms - isolating the hang to the WS multiplexer's aiohttp-frame-to-websockets-client round-trip per message. Reporter shipped a fork with --cdp-mode=direct (a per-Chromium TCP byte relay with no WebSocket-protocol awareness, 'so it cannot reproduce the multiplexer's framing bug') and offered an ~80 LoC PR. Filed 2026-05-25, never answered.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: internal/serve/wsproxy.go is structurally the same component - a WebSocket multiplexer re-framing CDP between a driver and per-seed Chromes - and cuttle's default driver is playwright-cli over connectOverCDP. The specific bug (framing/fragmentation differences that a raw-WS client tolerates and Playwright does not) is a real hazard, and the diagnostic that isolates it is cheap: run the same Target.getTargets probe through a raw WS client and through Playwright and compare. cuttle already carries one Playwright-specific CDP workaround (the service_worker browserContextId stamp for the connectOverCDP crash), which suggests this surface is exactly as fragile as the reporter found.

items.what: Maintainer explains WHY a second CDP endpoint breaks a Playwright-managed browser: launch_persistent_context connects over --remote-debugging-pipe (stdio), and adding --remote-debugging-port=9222 gives Chrome a second endpoint - 'Chrome accepts both, but when an external client connects to port 9222, Playwright's internal session management gets disrupted - the browser loses the ability to load pages, and the state doesn't recover even after disconnecting.' The prescribed answer is a separate daemon (cloakserve) that launches Chrome directly with no Playwright in the middle.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Independent confirmation of cuttle's core rule - the daemon owns Chrome, drivers only ever attach - and a precise, quotable explanation of what breaks when an agent ignores it and launches its own browser. This is exactly the failure the cuttle skill warns against ('Attach to cuttle's warm session - never launch a fresh browser or new profile'); this thread supplies the mechanism, which is far more persuasive to an LLM than a bare instruction. Good candidate for a line in internal/cli/SKILL.md.

items.what: Maintainer states that page.exposeFunction/exposeBinding and page.on('console') are DELIBERATELY disabled for stealth: the binding is 'observable from the page' and 'Antibot systems (Cloudflare, DataDome) detect Runtime.enable activity through console message serialization side effects.' Offered workaround is a userland console.log override polled via evaluate. Separately, the WebAuthn half was solved by config, not a patch: virtual authenticators with transport:'usb' get an all-zeros AAGUID (which Google rejects for passkeys) because Chrome erases it for usb/nfc/ble, while transport:'internal' preserves it - upstream Chromium behavior, plus a note that instant CDP acceptance of the prompt is itself timing-detectable.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Two things cuttle needs. First, Runtime.enable is a live detection vector - anything in internal/serve/ that enables Runtime broadly (or a driver that does) is paying a stealth cost, and cuttle's isolated-world probes should be audited for whether they force it. Second, the transport:'internal' AAGUID trick is a free unlock for passkey/2FA login flows in persistent seed profiles, which is squarely in cuttle's persistent-login use case. The 'accepting a prompt in milliseconds is detectable' note also generalizes: cuttle's humanize layer should apply a delay to any CDP-side prompt acceptance, not just to clicks.

items.what: Running the container on an ARM64 macOS host with --fingerprint-platform=windows leaks arm_64 through navigator.userAgentData's high-entropy architecture hint - 'incoherent as Windows typically runs on x86_64, and is an easy sign of automation.' Maintainer confirmed there is no flag to override the architecture hint alone; the only reliable fix is running an x86_64 build under Rosetta/QEMU. Coherent-Windows-on-ARM64 is 'on our roadmap'.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: This validates cuttle's arch-pinning rule (Windows persona on amd64, Apple Silicon persona on arm64) as the correct design rather than a limitation - it is precisely the incoherence cuttle refuses to create. Worth capturing as a documented invariant in the fingerprint package and in docs/UPGRADE.md's real-amd64 deployment gate rationale, since a future 'let me force a Windows persona on my M-series laptop' request would reintroduce a known-fatal tell.

items.what: A user generating a fresh profile + fresh proxy per run found FingerprintJS still linked every session back to the same VPS whenever Xvfb was used. Maintainer's diagnosis: --fingerprint-noise=false disables per-profile randomization of canvas and audio, which are what dominate FPJS's visitorId - 'across three fresh persistent-context profiles with noise=false, the canvas and audio fingerprints were identical every time.' The headless-vs-headed difference the user believed in was a red herring; the noise flag was the only variable that mattered. Screen dimension pins were explicitly ruled out as a cause.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: The multiplexer's entire premise is that one Chrome per fingerprint seed yields unlinkable identities. This thread is the specific way that promise silently breaks - if canvas/audio noise is off or seeded identically, every seed collapses to one device hash regardless of separate profiles, separate proxies and separate screen tables. Directly checkable against internal/fingerprint/args.go and the clark patch series, and a good candidate for an assertion in packages/browser/validate: launch two seeds, confirm canvas and audio hashes differ.

items.what: Clean A/B on one AWS EC2 Windows VM: deviceandbrowserinfo.com's hasInconsistentTimingResolution fires TRUE under CloakBrowser and FALSE under plain unpatched Playwright Chromium on the identical machine - isolating the signal to the stealth patches themselves, not the OS, hypervisor, or spoofing. Every other signal was clean, so this one flag alone flipped isBot to true. Maintainer confirmed and shipped a fix in a Preview build, noting 'This detector has been tightening its timing checks recently.'
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: The stealth patch series can BE the tell. cuttle runs clark's series forked verbatim at chromium-v148.0.7778.96-stealth5 and deliberately omits two of clark's later patches (0027-analyser-node-noise, 0047-suppress-cdc-globals) - which makes the A/B methodology here the important takeaway: packages/browser/validate should run cuttle against plain stock Chromium on the same host and diff detector output, so a patch that introduces a signal is caught the way the golden catches arg drift. This user's setup is the cheapest possible version of that harness.

items.what: Precise, reproducible divergence: real Chrome (non-incognito) sets navigator.storage.estimate().quota to exactly usage + 10GiB and keeps that delta constant as IndexedDB grows or shrinks; the patched binary sets quota to a flat 10GiB ignoring usage, so the delta drifts below 10GiB as soon as anything is stored. Related #320 (25 comments) shows the downstream cost - users fighting FingerprintJS 'incognito: true' on persistent contexts, passing --fingerprint-storage-quota=500 then 5000, getting nondeterministic results ('the first time incognito = false, but the second time = true').
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Storage quota is the primary incognito tell, and cuttle's persistent-login pitch dies if seeds read as incognito. The fix is precise and testable: quota must track usage + a constant, not be a constant. Checkable against the clark patch series in packages/browser/patches and assertable in packages/browser/validate. The #320 thread is also a warning about the failure mode - a flaky signal that flips run to run is far more expensive to debug than a consistently wrong one.

items.what: Request for a native omnibar profile identity chip - a grey pill like 'GPM | 0003' rendered inside the location bar by a Chromium UI patch, driven by --stealth-profile-label / --stealth-profile-code / --stealth-profile-tooltip switches. Motivation: operators running 20-30 profiles at once cannot tell the windows apart. Explicit non-goals: no extension badge (detectable, needs the extension subsystem, cannot render in the URL field), no DOM injection. Key property: it lives in browser chrome only, so it is invisible to page JavaScript.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle fronts N per-seed Chromes on ONE KasmVNC viewer at 127.0.0.1:6080. A human taking a captcha handoff, or an agent screenshotting the framebuffer, currently has no in-picture way to tell which seed a window belongs to. A seed label in the omnibar (or the window title, which is far cheaper than a Views patch and equally page-invisible) makes the viewer legible and makes screenshots self-documenting. The 'browser chrome only, never DOM' constraint is the load-bearing insight and is exactly right for cuttle's threat model.

items.what: A user's Show-and-tell describing the workflow they actually wanted for agents: pair the stealth browser with a persistent runtime so one browser launches once and stays alive across every agent call, exposing a tiny verb set - goto(), text(), links(pattern=), fill(), click(), tables() - with 'No cold starts. No re-launching Chromium. No re-passing bot detection on every call. Stay logged in across sessions.'
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle already delivers the hard half (warm per-seed pool, immortal keep-alive tab, persistent profiles, auth-state snapshot/restore). What this user built on top is the missing readable half, and the verb list is a better-validated spec than any feature request: text(), links(pattern=) and tables() are the page-comprehension primitives that make an agent stop guessing - the same gap as #274's `dump` and the direct antidote to cuttle's pain #3 and #4. Notably nobody in this ecosystem asks for a screenshot verb; they ask for structured text.

items.what: Cookie/CMP consent overlays rendering broken - Stack Overflow's banner layout-truncated, and onetrustdemo.com going entirely black because the overlay's mask renders without the dialog. The reporter found the workaround: open devtools, toggle to phone mode and back to desktop mode, and the popup renders correctly. Maintainer could not reproduce and attributed it to display scaling / regional CMP variants; the reporter maintained 'All secondary pop ups have this issue' after a clean profile.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: The workaround is the tell - toggling device emulation forces a resize/relayout, which means the failure is a viewport/DPR/emulation coherence bug, not a CMP bug. cuttle sets per-page Emulation overrides (setFocusEmulationEnabled, setLocaleOverride) on top of a window sized to the seed's spoofed screen inside a fixed 1920x1080 framebuffer - the same class of mismatch. A full-screen black mask with no visible dialog is also precisely the state that leaves an agent blind and poking a dead page (pain #4), so it is worth reproducing against cuttle deliberately.

items.what: Request for a one-command sanitized diagnostics bundle (version, OS/arch, engine version, enabled config, memory/perf stats, recent logs, crash reports) with explicit scrubbing of cookies, tokens, passwords, history, PROXY CREDENTIALS and API keys, so a bug report is complete on the first round-trip instead of after days of back-and-forth. Unanswered.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle has `status` and `logs` as separate verbs and a public repo whose non-negotiables forbid leaking infra references or credentials - which makes a scrub-by-construction diagnostics bundle a natural fit rather than a new subsystem. The credential-scrubbing list matters specifically because cuttle handles proxy credentials in two places (internal/fingerprint/proxy.go strips them from args, and the daemon answers proxy-407 over CDP), so any diagnostic dump is a live leak risk that has to be designed, not bolted on.

community.headline: CloakBrowser-Manager is the closest public analogue to cuttle's container half: stealth Chromium on KasmVNC/Xvnc, one profile per fingerprint, CDP exposed per profile, driven by Playwright. Its 52 issues and 15 PRs are almost entirely about the seams cuttle is hitting right now - the browser window not matching the framebuffer (PR #47 fixes it with `Browser.setWindowBounds`), the VNC viewer dropping and never reconnecting (#51, #35), clipboard being the only viable secret/CJK input path and it being half-broken (#2, #9, #7), and the single highest-signal finding in the repo: KasmVNC's virtual pointer has no X `device_type`, so `matchMedia('(pointer: fine)')` and `(hover: hover)` return false and every fingerprint suite flags the session as tampered (#8) - fixed upstream with a one-hunk Chromium patch that cuttle's 24-patch series does not carry. The direction of travel is a wholesale retreat from the noVNC-plus-translation-bridge architecture: the in-flight PR #50 rips the RFB relay out entirely, serves KasmVNC 1.5's own matched client behind nginx, and adds the affordances cuttle lacks - a tab manager, a downloads file browser, idle-timeout auto-stop, cold-CDP auto-launch, cookie warmup, extension install, and Widevine. Two sibling-repo threads (CloakBrowser #504, #507) name cuttle's dialog blindness and a latent isolated-world staleness bug in `humanize.go` precisely.

items.what: KasmVNC's virtual pointer is created without an X device_type, so Chromium's x11_hotplug_event_handler.cc never classifies it as a mouse. Result: matchMedia('(pointer: fine)') and matchMedia('(hover: hover)') both return false in the VNC session, and fingerprint.com / IPHey flag the browser as 'browser tampering' + incognito. Reporter traced it to the exact Chromium source line; maintainer confirmed 'this is a real detection vector' and shipped patch 045, which defaults an unrecognized pointer device to DEVICE_TYPE_MOUSE when (type == x11::Atom::None && device.use == IsXExtensionPointer). Reporter confirmed those were the ONLY two indicators that leaked.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle has exactly this exposure and no patch for it. ~/Projects/cuttle/packages/browser/patches/ contains 24 clark patches, none touching x11_hotplug_event_handler.cc or pointer/hover media queries (grep for DEVICE_TYPE_MOUSE returns nothing repo-wide). ops/docker/bin/docker-entrypoint.sh runs KasmVNC's Xvnc when CUTTLE_VNC=1 and bare Xvfb otherwise - Xvfb has no pointer device at all, so the default prod image is likely worse, not better. This is a two-line addition to the patch series that closes a leak visible to any commercial detector, and it regenerates cleanly through `just parity-golden` since it touches no arg-building.

items.what: PR 'fix: constrain browser window to VNC framebuffer' adds _fit_window_to_vnc(): right after launch, open a CDP session on the first page, call Browser.getWindowForTarget, and if left!=0 or top!=0 or left+width > framebuffer_width or top+height > framebuffer_height, issue Browser.setWindowBounds with {left:0, top:0, width, height} sized to the profile's screen. Wrapped in try/except with a warning log so a failure never blocks launch. Ships with a regression test that mocks the two CDP round-trips.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: This is cuttle agent-pain #1 verbatim. internal/fingerprint/ sizes --window-size to the seed's spoofed screen while ops/docker pins the framebuffer at 1920x1080 (Xvnc -geometry 1920x1080 / Xvfb -screen 0 1920x1080x24), so a seed with a smaller spoofed screen leaves the window floating in a corner of the viewer. The entrypoint's current answer is --start-maximized plus openbox, which fights the fingerprint layer rather than reconciling with it. A post-launch Browser.setWindowBounds pass in internal/serve (where the pool already owns a CDP session per instance) pins the window to (0,0) without changing the spoofed screen the page sees. The cleaner variant: size the Xvnc/Xvfb geometry per seed instead of a fixed 1920x1080.

items.what: Large in-flight PR replacing KasmVNC 1.3.3 + noVNC + a Python RFB translation bridge with KasmVNC 1.5.0's own matched web client behind an nginx data plane, so no framebuffer bytes traverse the app process. Ships server-authoritative encoding on the Xvnc command line: 30 FPS cap, dynamic quality 6-8, video-mode downscale to 1600x900 under motion, WebP, -IgnoreClientSettingsKasm; quality presets text/balanced/low/motion; opt-in in-band H.264/H.265/AV1 via WebCodecs; DRI3 (-hw3d -drinode) auto-enabled when an open-driver render node exists and skipped on proprietary NVIDIA; -PublicIP 127.0.0.1 to kill the STUN outbound lookup. Maintainer notes the binary's -videoCodec default is empty despite the man page claiming 'auto', and that -RectThreads parses but is dead in 1.5.0.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's ops/docker/Dockerfile installs the KasmVNC bookworm .deb plus a separate noVNC tarball and a hand-rolled ops/docker/bin/vnc-viewer.html that re-implements BinaryClipboard framing against noVNC's _normalMsg contract - the exact 'generic client + translation glue' shape this PR concluded was a mistake. cuttle's Xvnc invocation carries zero encoding flags, so quality/FPS are whatever the default is. The cheapest steal is the flag set alone (FPS cap + dynamic quality + video-mode downscale), which is a one-line entrypoint change; the -PublicIP 127.0.0.1 STUN suppression is also a free egress/stealth win for a container that should make no outbound lookups of its own.

items.what: 'Manager VNC viewer disconnects routinely and never reconnects.' Two compounding causes, root-caused in detail: (1) uvicorn is started with no --ws-ping-* flags so the default 20s ws_ping_timeout applies, and any event-loop stall past 20s (launching a second profile, a heavy workflow, the host sleeping) makes uvicorn reap the LIVE viewer socket even though Chrome and Xvnc are healthy; (2) the frontend's disconnect handler calls onDisconnect(), which unmounts the viewer back to the profile-edit form - so the first drop is terminal. Suggested fixes: raise ws-ping-timeout, move automation off the serving loop, and on disconnect probe GET /api/profiles/{id} - only fall back to teardown if status != running, otherwise reconnect with exponential backoff plus instant reconnect on visibilitychange/online and a manual retry button. PR #50 implements the frontend half as a useViewerSession state machine: 250ms->15s backoff with full jitter, offline/visibility handling, status-probe classification, and a dimmed keep-last-frame overlay, with the explicit invariant 'a network drop never stops the browser or navigates away'.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's ops/docker/bin/vnc-viewer.html connects noVNC straight to Xvnc's websocket with no reconnect logic at all - a laptop sleep, a backgrounded tab, or a docker network blip ends the human-handoff session, which is precisely when a human is mid-captcha. cuttle's daemon is Go so the event-loop-stall half does not apply, but the client-side invariant does: keep the last frame, dim it, reconnect with jittered backoff, reconnect immediately on visibilitychange/online, and never tear down the page on a socket close. That is ~40 lines in vnc-viewer.html and it directly hardens the human-handoff path the whole VNC feature exists for.

items.what: Maintainer's post-mortem on VNC freezing during video/animation: KasmVNC emits ~1,900 WebSocket messages/sec at 1920x1080, and on a fast local connection the bottleneck is the client's render speed, not the network - input still reaches the server, so the session only LOOKS dead, which is why switching profiles (forcing a reconnect) instantly 'unfreezes' it. Two attempted fixes failed and the maintainer says why: proxy-side frame dropping is impossible because WebSocket messages are arbitrary chunks of the continuous RFB byte stream, not frames, so dropping one corrupts the display; and WebSocket backpressure tuning does nothing when the network is not the constraint. A community member then found the concrete failure: the proxy treated msg[0] of EVERY WebSocket frame as an RFB message type, so a compressed Tight/JPEG chunk that happened to start with byte 180 (0xB4) was misread as BinaryClipboard and silently dropped, desynchronising noVNC into 'Unsupported encoding: -<redacted-id>'.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Two things. First, the diagnosis validates cuttle's architecture - vnc-viewer.html parses BinaryClipboard statefully inside noVNC's _normalMsg contract (returning false until the whole message is buffered) and the browser talks to Xvnc directly with no relay in between, so cuttle cannot hit the 0xB4 desync. Worth knowing that the stateful parse is load-bearing, not incidental, before anyone 'simplifies' it. Second, the freeze itself is unfixed at the client and only addressable server-side, which is the argument for adopting PR #50's Xvnc encoding flags (FPS cap + video-mode downscale) in cuttle's entrypoint rather than waiting for a viewer-side fix that cannot exist.

items.what: Clipboard is the community's de-facto secret/text injection channel, and it is the most-reported broken thing in the repo. #2: clipboard sync was off by default and required a toolbar click every session; maintainer's diagnosis names the two silent killers - the Clipboard API requires a secure context (HTTPS or literal localhost, so a plain http://IP access silently blocks navigator.clipboard.readText() with no error) and Safari rejects repeated reads even with a user gesture. Requester asked for a VNC_CLIPBOARD_DEFAULT env var; maintainer went further and made it a per-profile persisted 'Enable clipboard sync by default in VNC viewer' toggle defaulting to on. #9: on macOS over Chrome via 127.0.0.1 (so both causes ruled out) only the FIRST copy ever propagates - every later copy re-delivers the first one; maintainer conceded it as a repeated-copy limitation of the Dockerized VNC clipboard path and steered the user to native mode instead of fixing it. #35: the viewer randomly kicks back to the settings page 'more frequently when pressing Ctrl+V', tying the clipboard path to the disconnect bug.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: This is cuttle agent-pain #2 from the human side. cuttle's vnc-viewer.html implements both clipboard directions by hand over KasmVNC BinaryClipboard type 180, and inherits the same landmines: it is served over plain HTTP on 127.0.0.1:6080 (fine today, silently broken the moment anyone port-forwards it to a LAN IP), and there is no per-seed persistence or default-on state. The repeated-copy staleness in #9 is worth actively testing against cuttle's implementation - if cuttle's send path has the same bug, an operator pasting a second credential silently pastes the first one, which is a security-relevant failure, not a usability one.

items.what: 'Input method problem': CJK (Chinese/Japanese/Korean) text cannot be typed into a VNC-viewed browser at all. Maintainer's explanation is the best architectural answer in the repo: IME composition combines multiple keystrokes into one character through a candidate window, and it breaks at two levels - noVNC does not handle IME composition events so raw keystrokes go through uncomposed, and KasmVNC 1.3.3 has a known CJK keysym bug that freezes input entirely after several unconverted pinyin characters. Declared a structural limitation of the VNC architecture, with clipboard paste as the only workaround.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's humanize layer rewrites Input.insertText into real per-rune keystrokes up to 80 runes (internal/serve/humanize.go). For CJK, Cyrillic, Arabic, or any text a real user would compose via IME, that rewrite is actively wrong: real Chrome delivers those as composition/insertText events, not as a keystroke stream, so cuttle's humanization produces input that is both unfaithful to a human and potentially garbled. cuttle needs a script-aware bail-out - if the payload is outside the Latin/QWERTY-typeable set, pass Input.insertText through untouched rather than synthesising keystrokes it has no keyboard model for.

items.what: PR #50's README documents why downloads need explicit handling and what the residual traps are: Playwright intercepts EVERY download via CDP once a browser is under its control - including ones a human triggers by clicking in the VNC window, not just scripted ones - and by default saves the artifact under a random GUID name in a directory deleted the moment the profile stops. The fix points Playwright's artifact path at a hidden .pw-downloads staging dir inside the profile and copies each completed download out to a real ~/.../profiles/<id>/Downloads/ under its suggested filename, with Chrome-style (1)/(2) numbering. Two caveats stated plainly: a headless profile driven by a raw CDP client that never establishes a Playwright driver session can report the download CANCELED (a Chromium headless quirk), and a second Playwright driver connecting via connect_over_cdp() RESETS the browser's download destination to its own default - so external automation must use download.save_as() rather than relying on the manager's handler. PR #50 also adds a DownloadsBrowser file-manager UI with per-file save/delete and a zip-all endpoint.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: internal/serve/downloads.go already pins downloads into the seed's profile dir and serves them over GET /downloads and /downloads/{name}, so cuttle has the shape right. The new intel is the second-driver caveat: cuttle is a MULTIPLEXER, so a second driver attaching to the same seed is the normal case, not the exotic one. If cuttle sets the download path via Browser.setDownloadBehavior at launch, a playwright-cli or browser-use client attaching later can silently override it and cuttle's /downloads listing goes empty with no error. Worth verifying and, if confirmed, re-asserting setDownloadBehavior on every new client attach in the pool. The zip-all endpoint is also a cheap agent-ergonomics win over the current one-file-at-a-time verb.

items.what: PR #50 adds a TabManagerPanel plus api.listTabs(profileId) / api.closeTab(profileId, index) endpoints: a per-profile list of open tabs with titles and URLs and a close button on each, refreshed only when the panel opens or the running-profile set changes (deliberately NOT on the 3s poll tick, so an in-flight load is not reset on every render).
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle has no tab-list verb - the CLI surface is up/down/status/open/downloads/logs/purge-profile/context/skill. An agent that loses track of which tab it is on, or that a popup opened a fourth tab, has no way to ask. cuttle already proxies /json/list per seed in internal/serve/http.go and already filters the immortal keep-alive tab out of Target.getTargets in keepalive.go, so a `cuttle tabs [--close N]` verb is mostly plumbing over machinery that exists. This lands directly on the 'agents are blind to what the browser is actually showing' complaint.

items.what: PR #50 adds an idle-timeout sweeper with a carefully-reasoned definition of idle: a profile is stopped (cleanly, releasing its license claim) after N seconds with NO attached VNC viewer AND no CDP messages actually forwarded through the proxy - explicitly noting that 'a client attached but issuing no commands still counts as idle: only real traffic resets the clock, not the WebSocket's own keepalive pings'. Default 3600s via PROFILE_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, per-profile override, 0 to disable. Paired with the inverse affordance: hitting a STOPPED profile's CDP endpoint auto-launches it instead of answering 404, 'a safeguard for a CDP client that dials in cold'.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Both halves map onto cuttle's per-seed Chrome pool in internal/serve/. The cold-dial auto-launch is pure agent ergonomics: today an agent that attaches to a seed whose Chrome is not up gets a failure it has to interpret, when the daemon could just launch it - and cuttle already has launch backoff to make that safe. The idle definition is the subtler steal: cuttle's immortal keep-alive tab plus per-page focus-emulation pinning means a cuttle seed will happily hold RAM forever with nobody driving it, and 'keepalive pings do not count as traffic' is exactly the distinction a naive implementation gets wrong.

items.what: Maintainer design rationale for auth, worth reading in full: every route under /api/profiles/<id>/ authenticates on the profile id alone with no token, because 'a WebSocket handshake from Playwright, Puppeteer or chrome-remote-interface cannot carry an Authorization header, so a bearer token on that route means a patched client'. The uuid4 id is treated as a presigned-URL-grade capability (122 bits), with the honest caveats spelled out - it grants full control including DELETE, never expires, cannot be revoked without deleting the profile, and leaks through browser history, Referer, shared scrollback and pasted curl commands. The routes that would ENUMERATE ids (list, create) still require the token. Cross-origin WS is refused (Origin must match Host) so a hostile page cannot drive CDP even knowing the id. Separately, PR #48 (merged) removed /api/status from the auth-exempt set after finding it leaked running_count, binary_version, profiles_total and license tier to unauthenticated scanners fingerprinting exposed instances via fofa, replacing it with a bare /api/health for the Docker healthcheck.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle serve is loopback-only today and its docs treat the 127.0.0.1 port mapping as the security boundary (docker-entrypoint.sh says so explicitly for Xvnc). This thread is the map of what happens the moment anyone forwards that port, and it names the constraint that makes the obvious answer wrong: bearer tokens are unusable on a CDP endpoint because no stock driver can send the header. If cuttle ever grows remote access, per-seed capability URLs plus an Origin==Host check is the design that keeps playwright-cli / agent-browser / browser-use working unmodified. The #48 lesson applies right now: check whether cuttle's own status endpoint volunteers seed counts and versions to anything that can reach the port.

items.what: PR #50 adds backend/cookie_warmup.py: a 10-minute background pass that drives a brand-new profile through 20 curated high-traffic sites (google, youtube, wikipedia, amazon, reddit, nytimes, cnn, bbc, espn, ebay, walmart, target, imdb, weather, github, stackoverflow, a professional social network, twitter, instagram, spotify), one tab at a time with a dwell and a 20s load timeout, never raising on a site that fails. The stated rationale, in the module docstring: 'so a brand-new profile is not a completely blank slate of cookies and browsing history... this is about looking like a normal browsing history, not scraping anything.' Exposed as POST /api/profiles/{id}/cookie-warmup/start with a progress-reporting status endpoint and a frontend panel.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's internal/profile store gives each seed a persistent user-data-dir, but a freshly-created seed starts with zero cookies, zero history, and an empty Local State - a coherent, well-spoofed fingerprint attached to a browser that has demonstrably never been used. That combination is itself a signal to any detector scoring profile age. cuttle already has per-seed auth-state snapshot/restore over CDP, so it has the machinery to seed state; a `cuttle warmup <seed>` verb (or a first-launch hook) is a natural extension and is entirely independent of the browser patches. Note the site list is US-centric - cuttle's geoip-driven timezone/locale layer means the warmup list should follow the seed's locale, or the warmup itself becomes the incoherence.

items.what: A three-issue arc on extensions (#30 -> #37 -> #41) with an outstanding community answer. The reality established: Google blocks Web Store installs on ALL non-Chrome Chromium builds (Brave, ungoogled, AdsPower, CloakBrowser alike), and Chromium disabled .crx file installs globally around v75 - so the chrome://flags toggle and renaming a downloaded UUID file to .crx are both dead ends, and only unpacked --load-extension works. The five things that actually break an unpacked load: manifest.json must be at the root of the directory you point at (not the version-numbered parent), the path must be visible INSIDE the container, MV3 wallet extensions need headed mode because the service worker will not init under old headless, a profile previously launched without the extension can have Preferences that block it (wipe the profile once), and Windows->WSL->container bind mounts often produce unreadable permissions (chmod -R a+rX). Debug trick: open chrome://extensions with Developer mode on and open DevTools ON THAT PAGE - the console prints the real load-failure reason. #41 remains open with the harder symptom: with --load-extension set, the browser stops launching at all until the container is restarted, via the UI launch button as well as via Playwright.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle has no extension story at all, and the moment an agent needs uBlock, a captcha solver, or a wallet, every one of these traps applies to internal/fingerprint's arg-builder and the ops/docker image layout. The MV3-needs-headed point is already satisfied by cuttle (headed Chrome on Xvfb) and is a real advantage worth stating in SKILL.md. The stale-Preferences trap interacts directly with cuttle's persistent per-seed profile dirs and purge-profile verb. The chrome://extensions DevTools console trick is the kind of thing that belongs in cuttle's embedded SKILL.md so an agent can self-diagnose instead of guessing.

items.what: 'CDP port already in use when launching profiles immediately after stopping.' CDP port was computed as a static offset from the display number, so stopping a profile freed display :100, the next launch got :100 again, computed port 5100, and bind() failed because the kernel still held it in TIME_WAIT for 30-60s. Reporter notes the 3-attempt/3s retry loop cannot outlast TIME_WAIT, so in a pipeline where 8 browsers finish and 3 more start, the 3 always fail. Reporter proposed ephemeral bind(0); the maintainer explicitly chose NOT to, going with a rotating counter over a fixed 5100-5199 range instead, because 'keeps CDP ports in a predictable range for debugging and firewall rules' and a freed port is not retried for ~100 subsequent launches, well past any TIME_WAIT window.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's per-seed Chrome pool assigns a debugging port per instance and has launch backoff - the same TIME_WAIT trap applies to any seed that is stopped and immediately relaunched, which is exactly what `cuttle down` followed by `cuttle up` or a purge-profile cycle does. The maintainer's reasoning is the transferable part: a rotating counter over a bounded range beats both a static offset (collides) and bind(0) (unpredictable, undebuggable, un-firewallable) - and cuttle's whole value proposition is that everything is behind one predictable CDP port, so the internal per-seed ports being predictable-but-non-recycling fits the design.

items.what: A long debugging thread that ended in a self-retraction worth more than the original report. The reporter built an elaborate case that KasmVNC required a Sec-WebSocket-Origin header and that the Python websockets 16.0 library failed to send Origin, complete with source citations from both projects, a raw-socket repro, and a proposed aiohttp swap (plus the finding that the aiohttp session MUST be a lifespan singleton or connection-pool exhaustion crashes it after several connections). He then retracted the whole thing: the actual causes were (1) 'localhost' resolving to ::1 while the container only bound 0.0.0.0/IPv4, so browser WebSocket connections silently failed - use 127.0.0.1 - and (2) the launch endpoint returning 409 when the profile was already running, which the frontend treated as a hard failure and so never transitioned into the viewer. Maintainer-adjacent conclusion: return 200 with the running profile's info instead of 409.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Both real causes are live in cuttle. The IPv6 one: cuttle's docs and SKILL.md hand agents http://127.0.0.1:9222 and http://127.0.0.1:6080/ - keep it that way and say why, because any drift to 'localhost' in a driver command breaks silently and unforgettably on dual-stack hosts. The 409 one is an agent-ergonomics rule cuttle should hold itself to: `cuttle up` on an already-running seed, or an attach to a live instance, must be a success with the connection details, never an error the agent has to special-case - an LLM agent that gets a non-2xx will typically tear down and retry from scratch, which is the worst possible response to 'it already works'.

items.what: Sibling repo, directly on cuttle's dialog blindness: on Linux the native 'Open xdg-open?' external-protocol confirmation dialog appears when a page navigates to a custom scheme (zoommtg://) and BLOCKS the page's JS execution. The reporter tried and failed with all three of the obvious answers: --disable-features=ExternalProtocolDialog in launch args, context.route('zoommtg://**', route => route.abort()), and the Chrome Enterprise Policy AutoLaunchProtocolsFromOrigins written to /etc/opt/chrome/policies/managed/policy.json. Still open with no maintainer answer as of the window.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: This is cuttle agent-pain #4 with a concrete instance and a confirmed list of what does NOT work - saving the effort of trying all three. It also shows the class is broader than JS dialogs: alert/confirm/beforeunload are at least reachable over CDP (Page.javascriptDialogOpening / Page.handleJavaScriptDialog), but the external-protocol dialog is a native browser-process UI that CDP does not surface at all, so no amount of Page-domain handling sees it. For cuttle the practical implication is that any 'is the page blocked?' signal has to include a non-CDP check - the VNC framebuffer or a window-tree query via xdotool, both of which cuttle already has in the container - rather than assuming CDP can see everything that stops a page.

items.what: Sibling repo, and a near-exact description of a latent bug in cuttle's humanizer. After a refactor routed pre-click actionability checks through a CDP isolated world instead of plain Playwright reads, fill() started failing with ElementNotAttachedError for the full timeout on any element reached via a click- or form-driven navigation. Root cause: the isolated world was only invalidated from the goto path, and when the previous document survives in the BACK/FORWARD CACHE its isolated-world executionContextId stays VALID - so Runtime.evaluate keeps succeeding against the stale document rather than erroring, and the 'recreate on error' recovery path never fires. Reporter's three suggested fixes, in preference order: create the world with a non-empty worldName (Chromium recreates named worlds per document), invalidate on every navigation event rather than only on goto, or track the executionContextId/document identity per evaluate. Maintainer confirmed and fixed by refreshing the checks on every main-frame navigation, across Python sync+async, JS, and .NET.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: internal/serve/humanize.go is one of the two mitigations away from this exact failure. It DOES use a named world (const isolatedWorldName = "cuttle_probe"), which is the recommended fix - but isolatedWorld(sid) caches the executionContextId in h.worlds[sid] indefinitely and only drops it when Runtime.evaluate returns an error (evaluate() deletes the cache entry and probeWithRetry retries once). That is precisely the recovery mechanism this issue proves insufficient under bfcache: a bfcached document's context does not die, so the evaluate succeeds against the wrong document and no error ever triggers the rebuild. The consequence for cuttle is subtler than a raised exception - the pre-click settle gate samples elementFromPoint rects from a stale document and the post-click aria-toggle verify compares against stale attributes, so clicks get gated or re-fired on the wrong geometry with no error anywhere. Fix: invalidate h.worlds[sid] on Page.frameNavigated / Runtime.executionContextDestroyed events rather than relying on the evaluate error.

items.what: A cluster of detection reports and the maintainer's framing of them. #25/#24: fingerprint.com/playground flags 'incognito' and 'browser tampering' both from a bare ./chrome --fingerprint=4 launch and from the Manager. #18: IPHey reports 'detected anti-detect browser environment'. #23: a Mac user gets bot + VPN verdicts. Maintainer's answer on #23 does the useful separation: the VPN verdict is derived from the EXIT IP and is entirely independent of the browser fingerprint, so it will fire on any datacenter/VPN address regardless of how good the browser is - only a residential IP clears it - while the bot verdict was a stale-build problem. Notably #25/#24's incognito+tampering flags are the same symptom later root-caused in #8 as the KasmVNC pointer leak, and the reporter of #18 asked the others 'are you accessing the server via localhost?', hunting the same viewer-side cause.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Two things for cuttle's docs/STEALTH-VERIFICATION.md and the embedded SKILL.md. First, the exit-IP vs fingerprint separation is the single most common source of false 'cuttle's stealth is broken' reports, and stating it explicitly saves an agent from chasing the fingerprint layer when the proxy is the problem. Second, this cluster is the empirical evidence that the #8 pointer-device leak shows up in the wild as 'browser tampering' on mainstream detectors, not as some exotic edge case - it is what raises #8 from a curiosity to the highest-priority item in this whole report.

items.what: PR #50 auto-fetches the Widevine CDM on first container boot straight from Google's own component-update server (the same source Chrome uses; Linux x86-64 only, SHA-256 and CRX3-signature verified), in the background without blocking startup, cached on the data volume so it is fetched once ever rather than once per container, then seeded into each profile on its first launch. Disable via CLOAKBROWSER_FETCH_WIDEVINE=0 for air-gapped hosts or arm64, where Google publishes no CDM. The same PR's extension installer uses the identical mechanism to fetch a CRX by store id and strips the CRX2/CRX3 header, with an explicit SSRF note: the endpoint extracts only the 32-char id from a pasted URL and always builds its own request against Google's server.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's ops/docker image ships no Widevine CDM, so navigator.requestMediaKeySystemAccess('com.widevine.alpha') fails where real Chrome succeeds - a divergence that is cheap for a detector to probe and that cuttle's fingerprint layer cannot paper over, since it is a missing binary component rather than a spoofable value. The fetch-and-verify recipe here is directly reusable (and licence-clean: it is Google's own component server, not a vendored binary, which matters given cuttle's no-proprietary-binaries rule - though a CDM is proprietary, so this needs a deliberate call). Note the arm64 gap lands squarely on cuttle's macOS-persona arm64 image.

items.what: Two small human-handoff papercuts that recur. #32: the mouse cursor becomes invisible the moment the VNC viewer enters fullscreen - open, unfixed. #13: a feature request for session recording, argued for on the grounds that it is 'very useful when unattended'. #42: a request to start Xvnc lazily, only when the web UI is actually opened, from a user on a low-resource VPS paying for a display nobody is watching.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: All three land on cuttle's KasmVNC viewer (ops/docker/bin/vnc-viewer.html and the CUTTLE_VNC=1 entrypoint branch). The invisible-cursor bug is worth checking against cuttle's minimal viewer page since it strips the KasmVNC toolbar/UI and may or may not inherit the fix - a human taking over a captcha with no visible cursor is the failure mode that matters. Session recording is the more interesting one for an agent farm: an agent that ran unattended and failed leaves no visual record of WHY, and cuttle's answer today is `cuttle logs` plus whatever the driver captured. The lazy-Xvnc request is a non-issue for cuttle (the VNC branch is already opt-in behind CUTTLE_VNC=1) and is worth noting as a design cuttle already got right.

community.headline: clark-browser has effectively NO public conversations to mine: 3 issues total (all off-topic AI-written "partnership/market" pitches from one non-contributor, @foxtrot42mac, closed with zero maintainer replies), 0 pull requests ever, Discussions disabled, 0 commit comments, and 25 forks none of which have issues. 130 stars, single committer ("stan"), last push 2026-06-22. The signal that would normally live in issue threads instead lives in three maintainer-authored artifacts I mined in full: the 7 tagged release bodies (stealth0..stealth5), CHANGELOG.md (which contains an unusually candid "patches that were silently dead in 0.1.0" post-mortem plus an Unreleased section describing work never cut into a release), and specs/ + examples/ (the clean-room spec set and the agent-facing usage notes). Everything below is sourced from those, not from conversations, and nothing is inferred. Direction of travel: clark has moved past JS-surface fingerprinting into wire-level and automation-artifact territory - cdc_ global suppression aimed squarely at CDP clients, AnalyserNode audio noise, proxy-coherent WebRTC as a default, driver-viewport/seed coherence, and a TLS ClientHello measurement harness - and all of that landed AFTER the stealth5 tag that cuttle forked from, so cuttle is pinned to the last release before the interesting half.

items.what: Repo has no community conversation surface at all: issues #1/#2/#3 are AI-authored off-topic pitches ("LLM as search broker", "Data as commodity", "Voice Remote Control - partnership proposal") from a single non-contributor, all closed 2026-06-28 with one throwaway reply; zero PRs in repo history; Discussions disabled; zero commit comments; all 25 forks have issues disabled/empty.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Means there is no upstream bug-report channel to watch for clark regressions - cuttle cannot learn about a broken clark patch from clark's issue tracker. cuttle's own packages/browser/validate/smoke.py and the golden in internal/fingerprint/testdata/golden.json are the ONLY early-warning system; treat clark's release notes + CHANGELOG as the upstream feed instead of issues.

items.what: CHANGELOG 0.2.0 post-mortem: four patches were PRESENT in 0.1.0 but silently never fired at runtime. (a) navigator.platform was patched on NavigatorID::platform, but the JS-visible path is NavigatorBase::platform which short-circuits to GetReducedNavigatorPlatform() - a hardcoded host string. (b) navigator.hardwareConcurrency was patched on NavigatorConcurrentHardware, but NavigatorBase::hardwareConcurrency short-circuits to a hardcoded 2 when kReducedSystemInfo is on (which patch 0019 enables). (c) --fingerprint-timezone called icu::TimeZone::adoptDefault from RenderThreadImpl::Init, which changed ICU's default but did NOT invalidate V8's ICUTimezoneCache, so Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone kept returning the host zone; fixed by a blink::ClarkSetTimeZoneOverride bridge over TimeZoneController::SetTimeZoneOverride that intentionally leaks the RAII handle so the override outlives the call. (d) --fingerprint-* switches never reached renderers at all because RenderProcessHostImpl::AppendRendererCommandLine only forwards switches listed in kSwitchNames[] - fixed by 0050-renderer-arg-whitelist-fingerprint.patch.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle carries 0006, 0019, 0032 and 0050 verbatim, so it inherits both the bugs and the fixes - but the failure MODE is the lesson: a patch can apply cleanly, build, and pass the args-level golden while producing zero runtime effect. cuttle's golden.json only pins the argv cuttle emits; it proves nothing about what the binary does with those args. The guard that would have caught all four is a per-vector runtime JS assertion in packages/browser/validate/smoke.py (assert navigator.platform, hardwareConcurrency, Intl timezone, and a --fingerprint-* value actually observed in a renderer AND in a worker). Worth auditing that smoke.py asserts each of the 24 patches' JS surface, not a subset.
items.ref: CHANGELOG.md 0.2.0 "Patches that were silently dead in 0.1.0" - https://github.com/clark-labs-inc/clark-browser/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

items.what: Unreleased-only patch 0047-suppress-cdc-globals: a V8 extension registered at context creation that (1) pre-defines cdc_, __webdriver*, __selenium*, __driver_evaluate, __fxdriver_*, __lastWatirAlert/Confirm/Prompt as non-configurable, non-writable, non-enumerable undefined, and (2) monkeypatches Object.defineProperty to silently swallow any later definition whose key starts with cdc_, __webdriver, __selenium, or __$webdriver. The spec (specs/K-headless.md #47) states the rationale: Chromium injects window.cdc_<random> when CDP is open, DevTools does not actually depend on them, they are a Selenium-era vestige, and detection sites grep for them.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: This is the single highest-applicability upstream patch cuttle is missing. cuttle's entire architecture is CDP-open-by-design (internal/serve/pool.go launches every seed with --remote-debugging-port and every driver attaches over it), and drivers cuttle blesses (playwright-cli, agent-browser, browser-use) are exactly the class of client that injects these globals. The defineProperty interceptor matters more than the pre-definition: it blocks globals injected AFTER context creation, i.e. by the attached driver mid-session, which a startup-time strip would miss. packages/browser/versions.env already documents 0027/0047 as a deliberate post-stealth5 divergence to cherry-pick - this is the argument for doing it, and 0047 should be cherry-picked ahead of 0027.

items.what: Unreleased-only patch 0027-analyser-node-noise: seed-derived per-bin scale+offset on RealtimeAnalyser's getFloatFrequencyData/getByteFrequencyData in third_party/blink/renderer/modules/webaudio/realtime_analyser.cc. CHANGELOG 0.2.0 had explicitly listed this as a KNOWN GAP: "Audio noise covers only AudioBuffer::getChannelData and copyFromChannel. AnalyserNode.getFloatFrequencyData() and MediaStreamAudioSourceNode routes are not yet perturbed" - i.e. a detector reading the frequency domain instead of the destination buffer bypassed patch 0026 entirely. Note the related 0026 gotcha documented in the same changelog: 0026 hooks ONLY the ExceptionState overload of getChannelData, because the no-exception-state overload is also called by SharedAudioBuffer setup BEFORE the audio thread fills the buffer, so hooking it there latches "already noised" on an empty buffer and the renderer overwrites the noise.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle ships 0026 but not 0027 (packages/browser/patches/ has 0026-audio-fingerprint-noise.patch, no 0027), so cuttle's audio fingerprint is defeated by any detector that goes through AnalyserNode - a documented, named bypass of a patch cuttle does ship. MediaStreamAudioSourceNode is still unpatched upstream too, so that route remains open for both. Cherry-pick target alongside 0047.

items.what: The launcher now DEFAULTS webrtc_policy to "proxy-coherent" whenever a proxy is configured, setting both --force-webrtc-ip-handling-policy=disable_non_proxied_udp and --webrtc-ip-handling-policy=disable_non_proxied_udp. Explicit param or CLARK_WEBRTC_POLICY still wins. It shipped as opt-in in stealth2/stealth4 and was promoted to a proxy-triggered default in the unreleased commit. The stealth4 release note adds an operational caveat: their WebRTC smoke's raw control gathered no ICE candidates at all inside an AWS Docker network, so the harness reports that as a warning unless CLARK_WEBRTC_REQUIRE_RAW_CANDIDATES=1 - i.e. "no leak observed" in a container can be a false pass.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle handles WebRTC purely at the patch level: internal/fingerprint/proxy.go ResolveWebRTCArgs rewrites --fingerprint-webrtc-ip=auto to the resolved proxy exit IP, and there is no --webrtc-ip-handling-policy / --force-webrtc-ip-handling-policy anywhere in the tree (grep confirms zero hits). Those are complementary, not redundant: spoofing the reported IP does not stop Chromium from gathering a genuinely non-proxied UDP route, which is a separate observable. Adding both switches when a seed has a proxy is a few lines in internal/fingerprint/args.go/proxy.go. The false-pass caveat also applies directly to cuttle's own container smoke.

items.what: Driver-viewport/seed coherence: the launcher pins --fingerprint-screen-width/height from a seed-hashed pool (1920x1080, 1536x864, 2560x1440, 1366x768, 1440x900) that "must match the C++ pool in patches/000-shared/clark_seed.cc", and get_viewport_from_args() derives the Playwright viewport as screen.width x (screen.height - taskbar) with PLATFORM_TASKBAR_HEIGHTS = {windows: 48, macos: 95, linux: 0}, replacing a hardcoded 1920x947 default in launch_context/launch_persistent_context. Stated rationale in the code comment: "the Playwright viewport and the binary's screen.width/height never disagree".
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle already does the launch half of this (internal/fingerprint/args.go:354-357 emits --fingerprint-screen-width/height plus --window-size = screen minus taskbar, pinned by golden.json screen_args), so the arg layer is covered. The uncovered half is the DRIVER layer: cuttle hands drivers a bare CDP endpoint, and playwright-cli / agent-browser / browser-use each apply their own default viewport or none on attach, so window.innerWidth can disagree with the seed's spoofed screen.* - the exact incoherence clark went out of its way to close. Two concrete cuttle actions: (1) surface the seed's screen/window size in `cuttle status` and in internal/cli/SKILL.md so an attaching driver is told what viewport to use, and (2) for pain #1 (window does not fill the VNC viewer), the framebuffer is fixed 1920x1080 while a seed may draw 1366x768 - either size the Xvfb/KasmVNC framebuffer per-seed from the same screen table, or bias the seed pool toward 1920x1080 for VNC-visible seeds.
items.ref: commit e7e8a57a, clarkbrowser/config.py get_viewport_from_args / SCREEN_SIZE_POOL / PLATFORM_TASKBAR_HEIGHTS - https://github.com/clark-labs-inc/clark-browser/commit/e7e8a57a

items.what: clarkbrowser/hygiene.py - assess_launch_hygiene() returns typed findings for launch-arg footguns, gated by CLARK_LAUNCH_HYGIENE = warn|strict|off (strict raises). Codes: enable-automation (user args re-added --enable-automation), devtools-open (--auto-open-devtools-for-tabs / --devtools), devtools-kwarg (Playwright devtools=True), remote-debugging-public-address (CDP bound off loopback), remote-debugging-implicit-address (--remote-debugging-port with no explicit --remote-debugging-address), remote-allow-origins-wildcard (--remote-allow-origins=*). The docstring is explicit that this "does not hide or bypass anything" - it catches accidental settings that make runs brittle or easy to misdiagnose. IGNORE_DEFAULT_ARGS is likewise pinned to ["--enable-automation", "--enable-unsafe-swiftshader"] with the comment "Playwright default args we suppress - they leak automation signals".
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle has an arg-passthrough path (internal/serve/pool.go:478-486 appends caller args after the seed's own, with --window-size dedupe) and no validation on what a caller passes through - an agent adding --enable-automation or --auto-open-devtools-for-tabs silently degrades every seed with no signal. cuttle would also trip clark's own remote-allow-origins-wildcard check today (pool.go emits --remote-allow-origins=* alongside --remote-debugging-address=127.0.0.1, as does validate/smoke.py:193-194). A small hygiene gate in the serve daemon - warn in logs, or refuse under a strict flag - is directly portable and is the kind of thing that turns a silent stealth regression into a visible one.

items.what: clarkbrowser/interaction.py - InteractionPacer / AsyncInteractionPacer, described in the changelog as keeping "agent clicks from bursting faster than the page can reasonably respond". Design: min_interval_ms=350 between any two actions, same_target_cooldown_ms=900 for repeated clicks on the SAME target, jitter_ms=200 - and critically, jitter is added ONLY when a wait was already required (delay > 0), so an agent that is naturally slow pays nothing. Seeded RNG for reproducibility. The whole thing is ~140 lines and deliberately not a mouse-path simulator.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Two things for internal/serve/humanize.go. First, the cost complaint: cuttle pays ~0.5s per click and ~130ms/char unconditionally; clark's "only pay when you would otherwise be too fast" rule is a direct model for making cuttle's settle gate and curved-mouse path conditional on the observed inter-action gap - if the agent already waited 2s since the last Input event, the human-timing budget is already satisfied and the expensive path can be skipped. Second, the 900ms same-target cooldown is a re-click-storm guard that sits right next to cuttle's post-click aria-toggle verify-and-re-click: cuttle re-clicks a swallowed click, but has no floor on how fast an agent can hammer the same element, which is both a detection signal and a source of double-submits.

items.what: examples/agent_browser.md "Practical notes" - the only agent-facing guidance in the repo, and the closest thing to "here is how LLM agents misuse this". Rules given: keep one identity stable for a session, do NOT rotate fingerprint/timezone/language/viewport/IP between clicks; match proxy geography and type to timezone, locale and network profile; restart the driver session after changing executable path, profile, proxy, User-Agent or fingerprint args (and run `agent-browser close --all` before switching executables); prefer `snapshot -i` plus @ref clicks for agent workflows; use screenshots for visual confirmation; keep WebGPU deliberately disabled in headless unless the coherent adapter-info patch is on; use a Linux persona on Linux unless a real Windows font pack is passed via --fingerprint-fonts-dir, "otherwise font enumeration exposes the host"; keep CDP bound to localhost because any process reaching the port controls the browser.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: This maps almost line-for-line onto internal/cli/SKILL.md, which is cuttle's contract with the agent. Three of these are gaps worth stating explicitly there: (1) "restart the driver session after changing X" - cuttle's seed identity is stable by construction, but an agent that reattaches with different driver flags mid-session gets incoherence cuttle will not warn about; (2) "prefer snapshot + @ref clicks, use screenshots for visual confirmation" is exactly the workflow cuttle's pain #3 (screenshots feel like a hassle) and pain #4 (agents blind to dialogs) are about - clark's answer is that the agent should be taking a screenshot as the confirmation step after every state-changing action, which is cheap guidance cuttle can bake into SKILL.md before it builds any screenshot verb; (3) the "do not rotate identity between clicks" warning is a good SKILL.md line given cuttle exposes multiple seeds behind one CDP port and nothing stops an agent from round-robining them.

items.what: Detection failure isolated to an HTTP header, not JS: the stealth1 live sweep failed Antoine Vastel's areyouheadless with an explicit "You are Chrome headless" verdict while passing SannySoft, BrowserLeaks Client Hints and BrowserLeaks WebGL. Follow-up A/B on the same released binary: without --accept-lang -> "You are Chrome headless"; with --accept-lang=en-US,en -> "You are not Chrome headless". Root cause written up in docs/bot-detection-results.md: "A Chrome-looking request without Accept-Language is classified as headless by that endpoint". Same sweep records CreepJS still showing a visible Headless panel (chromium: true, like-headless 0%) as the remaining backlog, and Incolumitas reporting connectionRTT FAIL (later addressed by 0051-network-information-profile).
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle already emits --accept-lang (internal/fingerprint/args.go acceptLangArg builds it from the seed's locale with a base-language fallback), so the specific fix is covered - but the methodology is the transferable part and cuttle has the identical blind spot class: cuttle's golden.json and validate/smoke.py both assert JS-visible surfaces, and neither captures the HTTP request headers the browser actually puts on the wire. This is the same shape as cuttle's own issue #24 (Sec-CH-UA headers absent on the wire despite a coherent navigator.userAgentData). A wire-level header capture in packages/browser/validate would catch both.

items.what: TLS/JA3-JA4 handled as measure-first, patch-maybe-never. specs/J-tls-http.md says "Defer this whole category until measured" with the reasoning: BoringSSL's default ClientHello IS Chrome's ClientHello because they are built together, same for HTTP/2 SETTINGS, so unless ungoogled-chromium made non-default changes there the fingerprint is inherited for free - if the captured hash matches real Chrome the patches are no-ops, ship without them. The unreleased commit then adds tests/tls_fingerprint.py, a 414-line harness that stands up a LOCAL TLS server (no network access needed), captures the raw ClientHello bytes the stealth binary emits, parses ciphers/extensions/curves into JA3 and JA4, compares against a real-Chrome-148 baseline via CLARK_EXPECTED_JA3/JA4, and prints the per-extension delta when it differs.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle has zero TLS-layer coverage - no ClientHello capture anywhere in packages/browser/validate, and no statement of whether the self-built ungoogled-148 binary's JA3/JA4 matches stock Chrome 148. Since cuttle builds its own binary rather than consuming clark's, that assumption is LESS safe for cuttle than for clark: the build driver in packages/browser/build/ picks its own GN args, and a flipped BoringSSL-adjacent flag would silently shift the wire fingerprint with nothing to catch it. The harness is self-contained and offline, so it drops into the validate/ harness cheaply, and the likely outcome (no delta) is itself the valuable result - it retires a whole category of speculative work.

items.what: Font-pack plumbing bug and its fix, spanning stealth2/stealth4: Linux launches were pairing a Windows UA/Win32 persona with a tiny Linux font set, so the launcher now defaults to a Linux-coherent profile unless a real Windows font pack is explicitly configured (CLARK_WINDOWS_FONTS_DIR / CLARK_LINUX_FONTS_DIR / CLARK_FINGERPRINT_FONTS_DIR). The sharper detail is in the 0.2.0 changelog: font directories were previously "only being passed as audit metadata" - the flag was set but Chromium never actually saw the fonts - fixed by adding target-platform font-dir validation plus generated Linux Fontconfig profiles. CHANGELOG still lists as a known gap that font enumeration depends on real installed fonts, with native FontCache plumbing and synthetic fallback metrics deferred.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle bakes persona fonts into the image at /opt/personafonts (ops/docker/, Windows pack for amd64, macOS pack for arm64 with Apple advance widths stamped from macfonts/metrics.json) and passes --fingerprint-fonts-dir. clark's bug is the exact failure mode cuttle is exposed to: the flag can be present and validated while Fontconfig never actually resolves the pack, and the only way to know is to measure enumeration and measureText widths in-browser rather than assert the flag. cuttle's README already argues that renaming alone is insufficient because detectors compare measureText against CSS generics - the missing piece is a runtime assertion in validate/smoke.py that the persona families both enumerate AND measure correctly inside the shipped container, per arch.

items.what: specs/K-headless.md #48 states the permissions gap more broadly than the shipped patch: stock headless Chromium returns state === 'denied' for MANY permissions when nothing was explicitly denied, and bot-detection literature flags 'denied' as suspicious. The spec's intended change covers notifications, geolocation, microphone, camera, clipboard-read and clipboard-write, with a loop test asserting each returns prompt|granted. The release notes only ever claim verification for the notifications pair (Notification.permission === 'default' AND permissions.query({name:'notifications'}) === 'prompt'), which was the original sannysoft HEADCHR_PERMISSIONS failure.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle ships both 0010-notification-permission-prompt and 0048-permissions-prompt-default, so the mechanism is present - but the verified surface upstream is notifications only. Worth a direct check in packages/browser/validate/smoke.py that geolocation, camera, microphone, clipboard-read and clipboard-write also return prompt on cuttle's own binary, since cuttle runs HEADED under Xvfb rather than headless=new and the headless-mode branch these patches key off may behave differently in that configuration - a case clark never tested because clark's whole validation path is headless.

community.headline: clearcote-browser is public with issues enabled (83 stars, 13 issues, 7 PRs, no Discussions), and every thread is high-signal — the maintainer (@pim97) writes multi-page technical replies that read like design docs, and two reporters (@ingepanch13011, @fetchhh) file forensic-grade fingerprint audits with control rows and repros. But the community here is fingerprint auditors, not agent builders: there is literally NOTHING about downloads, uploads, screenshots, native JS dialogs, cookie banners, popups/new tabs, VNC, or LLM-agent misbehaviour. What the conversations do deliver is a catalogue of "self-contradiction" bugs that need no reference corpus to detect — spoofed JS value vs unspoofed request header, canvas noise on a flat fill, a WebGL2 context advertising WebGL1 extensions, srflx ICE candidates with zero host candidates, a window wider than the screen it claims — plus a maintainer stance that suppression is worse than plumbing and that a build shipped without release optimisations is itself a timing signal. Several of these map to defects cuttle almost certainly shares today, because cuttle patches the same JS accessors clearcote patched and left the same header/network paths alone.

items.what: Client-hint request headers (Sec-CH-DPR, Sec-CH-Device-Memory) carry the HOST machine's real values while JS reports the persona's — a server that opts into client hints gets both sides of the same fact in one page load and sees them disagree. Reporter's control table shows JS deviceMemory=8 while the header says 32, on a bare launch with no fingerprint option at all. Maintainer found TWO producers for DPR: the browser process adds the hint on navigation from the real display scale factor, and the renderer adds it for fetches via FrameFetchContext::GetDevicePixelRatio() -> Document::DevicePixelRatio(), which is a DIFFERENT accessor from the LocalDOMWindow::devicePixelRatio getter the persona overrides. Their first fix changed nothing because they only patched one. Both now resolve through a single function. Crucially, the maintainer explicitly rejected suppression: 'we took plumbing rather than suppression ... a Chrome-branded build that omits a hint it advertises support for is its own anomaly.'
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle has the exact same shape of defect, verified by reading the patches. packages/browser/patches/0008-device-memory-from-cli.patch replaces only blink::NavigatorDeviceMemory::deviceMemory() (the JS accessor) and touches nothing in the header path. packages/browser/patches/0013-window-outer-and-dpr.patch patches only LocalDOMWindow::devicePixelRatio - the precise accessor clearcote proved is insufficient. And packages/browser/patches/0019-enable-ungoogled-stealth-features.patch flips kRemoveClientHints to FEATURE_ENABLED_BY_DEFAULT, i.e. cuttle chose exactly the suppression route the maintainer argues is its own anomaly.
